{"number":1676,"title":"Declarative checks: the four-moment design, the rule inventory, and pass two (derive → quantify)","body":"Closes #1675
Refs #1672

## What this is

The review the dispatch asked for, and the first phase of the mechanism it proposes.

- **`docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md`** — every rule in every pack's `RULES.md` (557 rows), classified by the moment that could carry it deterministically: **A** convertible with today's vocabulary (187), **B** two-pass derive→assert (51), **C** work scope (26), **D** action guard on a tool call (38), **E** transcript (23), **F** procedure with a nameable trigger → a skill loaded by it (61), **G** prose (131), **H** mis-homed (6), **X** already carried (34). Each row names the signature and what the mechanism lacks.
- **`docs/declarative-checks/DESIGN.md`** — the end state: four evaluation moments (world, work, action, trigger) declared in one JSON vocabulary; the two-pass world scope (named value sets, then quantifiers — the shape CodeQL predicates, Datalog, Rego, Semgrep join mode and Go analyzer facts all converged on, minus recursion); declarative work assertions; declared PreToolUse guards evaluated both at the hook and over the transcript at Stop; skill triggers on tool calls, owner phrases and tool results beside the existing file-edit paths; alternatives and their drawbacks; the retrospective brief.
- **The plan** is on #1672 (five phases, each an engine change every member receives).

## Phase 1, landed here

`engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs`: `extractValueSets` derives from lines (`fromLinesMatching` + `inFilesMatching`, `splitValuesOn`), tracked paths, added lines (work scope) and fanned-out parsed fields (`valuesAtFields`); every value carries its origin and the named groups that found it; `whenSetEmpty` can report the empty set. Pass two: `checkSetValues` (some file matches a filled template / none does / a path exists / a tracked path matches — with `valueIsPattern` for auditing other declarations' patterns), `checkSetPairs` (the join), `requireIdenticalFiles` (twins by basename). Line-derived sets fill during the one shared sweep, so a two-pass rule still costs one walk.

Proof against the real tree:

- `references-integrity` is now data (`packs/claudinite-growth/declared-checks.json`); its rule module is deleted and its fixtures kept.
- `doc-pointers-resolve` (new, blocking with grace) found **seven** rule modules across four packs whose `doc:` still named the pre-#385 `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` path — fixed here, each pack bumped with its row. The growth pack's two rows claiming `60903.5` are folded, which clears the `pack-version-claimed-once` red that was already on `main`.

## Verified

- `node --test engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs` — 111 pass, including the new two-pass cases; a mutation of the line collector fails six of them.
- The growth, basics, python and google-identity pack tests; `check_the_world` at 0 blocking on this branch.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub.

{"number":345,"title":"python: convert the lazy-import & install-hint rules into skill-owned check-the-work rules","body":"Reworks the new `python` pack to follow the pattern PR #350 established: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move every rule that has a false-positive-free file-scoped signature into check-the-work tests (deleting its prose so the failure message is the only copy), and keep as prose only the residue that genuinely has no such signature.

## What changed

**The pack keeps prose for the residue and now also mounts a skill.** `packs/python/pack.mjs` adds `skills: ['python-optional-deps']` (fingerprint `detect` unchanged); `RULES.md` is trimmed to the three judgment rules; `README.md`'s rule table shows how each rule is now enforced.

**New skill `python-optional-deps`** — a minimal SKILL.md (trigger + one pointer paragraph, no re-teaching so nothing drifts) and a `checks.mjs` owning two rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. A shared `pyproject.mjs` holds the packaging knowledge both rules need (the declared-optional dist set, and the conservative dist→import-name mapping) — kept beside the rules, not in `checks/lib` (which carries engine mechanism only, per #351).

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `python-optional-import-top-level` | blocking | a module-top-level (column-0, so outside any def/try) `import`/`from` of a package the repo's own `[project.optional-dependencies]` declares optional |
| `python-optional-import-install-hint` | advisory | a `try/except ImportError` guard whose try-body imports a declared-optional package and whose except-body re-raises with no `pip install` hint anywhere in it |

## Which converted, and why / what stayed prose

The strong ground truth is the project's own `pyproject.toml`: `[project.optional-dependencies]` names *exactly* which packages are optional, so no "is this heavy?" judgment is needed to gate rules 2 and 3 — a top-level import (or an unhelpful guard re-raise) of a self-declared-optional package is a false-positive-free, file-scoped signal. Both checks are inert unless the repo declares optional deps (the RELEVANCE-FIRST gate — a skill check runs on every repo), scope only to those exact packages, skip test files, and self-exclude the skill's own dir.

- **Rule 2 (import lazily)** → `python-optional-import-top-level`, **blocking**. A guarded top-level import is indented (never column 0), so it is *not* flagged here — that shape is rule 3's domain, keeping the two clean.
- **Rule 3's "re-raise names the extra"** → `python-optional-import-install-hint`, **advisory** (whether a message names the *exact* extra is a wording judgment). A block is in scope only when its own try-body imports a declared-optional package, so an unrelated `except ImportError` (a fallback import, a feature probe) is never touched.
- **Stayed prose (documented residue):** *which deps belong in the dependency-free base set* (rule 1) and *the stdlib-backend architecture* (rule 4) are genuine architecture judgment with no static signature; and *the `# noqa: F401` availability-probe suppression* (rule 3's other half) can't be told from an accidental unused import without a full unused-name analysis. A dist whose import name is unrelated to its name (`Pillow`→`PIL`) is deliberately unmapped — a safe false-negative, never a false-positive.

## Tests

17 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find with the right severity/line; clean ones (lazy in-function imports, guarded/indented imports, the grounded install-hint re-raise, probe guards with no raise, guards around non-optional imports, marker-less repos, `pyproject` with no optional-deps, test files, the skill's own dir) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering each `run()` fails exactly the two violating-fixture tests per rule). Full suite: **434 pass**. Whole-repo sweep: clean on content (the only finding is the pre-existing branch-update merge commit, which resolves on squash-merge). {"number":345,"title":"python: convert the lazy-import & install-hint rules into skill-owned check-the-work rules","body":"Reworks the new `python` pack to follow the pattern PR #350 established: keep the pack, add a skill for the activity, move every rule that has a false-positive-free file-scoped signature into check-the-work tests (deleting its prose so the failure message is the only copy), and keep as prose only the residue that genuinely has no such signature.

## What changed

**The pack keeps prose for the residue and now also mounts a skill.** `packs/python/pack.mjs` adds `skills: ['python-optional-deps']` (fingerprint `detect` unchanged); `RULES.md` is trimmed to the three judgment rules; `README.md`'s rule table shows how each rule is now enforced.

**New skill `python-optional-deps`** — a minimal SKILL.md (trigger + one pointer paragraph, no re-teaching so nothing drifts) and a `checks.mjs` owning two rules, discovered by `skills/registry.mjs` and run at every Stop and in CI. A shared `pyproject.mjs` holds the packaging knowledge both rules need (the declared-optional dist set, and the conservative dist→import-name mapping) — kept beside the rules, not in `checks/lib` (which carries engine mechanism only, per #351).

| Rule | Severity | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `python-optional-import-top-level` | blocking | a module-top-level (column-0, so outside any def/try) `import`/`from` of a package the repo's own `[project.optional-dependencies]` declares optional |
| `python-optional-import-install-hint` | advisory | a `try/except ImportError` guard whose try-body imports a declared-optional package and whose except-body re-raises with no `pip install` hint anywhere in it |

## Which converted, and why / what stayed prose

The strong ground truth is the project's own `pyproject.toml`: `[project.optional-dependencies]` names *exactly* which packages are optional, so no "is this heavy?" judgment is needed to gate rules 2 and 3 — a top-level import (or an unhelpful guard re-raise) of a self-declared-optional package is a false-positive-free, file-scoped signal. Both checks are inert unless the repo declares optional deps (the RELEVANCE-FIRST gate — a skill check runs on every repo), scope only to those exact packages, skip test files, and self-exclude the skill's own dir.

- **Rule 2 (import lazily)** → `python-optional-import-top-level`, **blocking**. A guarded top-level import is indented (never column 0), so it is *not* flagged here — that shape is rule 3's domain, keeping the two clean.
- **Rule 3's "re-raise names the extra"** → `python-optional-import-install-hint`, **advisory** (whether a message names the *exact* extra is a wording judgment). A block is in scope only when its own try-body imports a declared-optional package, so an unrelated `except ImportError` (a fallback import, a feature probe) is never touched.
- **Stayed prose (documented residue):** *which deps belong in the dependency-free base set* (rule 1) and *the stdlib-backend architecture* (rule 4) are genuine architecture judgment with no static signature; and *the `# noqa: F401` availability-probe suppression* (rule 3's other half) can't be told from an accidental unused import without a full unused-name analysis. A dist whose import name is unrelated to its name (`Pillow`→`PIL`) is deliberately unmapped — a safe false-negative, never a false-positive.

## Tests

17 new fixture tests (scratch-repo harness), each rule proven both directions — violating fixtures find with the right severity/line; clean ones (lazy in-function imports, guarded/indented imports, the grounded install-hint re-raise, probe guards with no raise, guards around non-optional imports, marker-less repos, `pyproject` with no optional-deps, test files, the skill's own dir) stay quiet — and mutation-tested red (neutering each `run()` fails exactly the two violating-fixture tests per rule). Full suite: **434 pass**. Whole-repo sweep: clean on content (the only finding is the pre-existing branch-update merge commit, which resolves on squash-merge). The `file-placement` `skills/` acceptance from #350 already covers the engine-lib import; catalogs (`packs/README.md` row, `skills/README.md` entry) updated for `catalog-completeness`, and the pack's `skills` list satisfies `skill-ownership`.

## 2026-07-19 · born · python pack: optional-dep discipline as skill-owned checks and residue prose (#345)
- **Source:** missingbulb/LaughCounter, whose stdlib-only core keeps the YAMNet/TensorFlow and
  Torch/SpeechBrain models behind `[project.optional-dependencies]` extras, imported lazily per
  backend.
- **Reason:** a declared-optional package imported at module top level runs at `import <pkg>` time,
  dragging the heavy or native stack into the dependency-free core and breaking every path for
  anyone who installed the package without that extra.
- **Actor:** the growth-discover run, merged by @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** claude, per the commit trailer.
- **Mechanism:** a blocking check of the skill. `[project.optional-dependencies]` is the only place
  a package is *declared* optional, so the repo's own `pyproject.toml` is the ground truth that
  makes the signature false-positive-free and lets the rule convert from prose at all; the gate is
  that declaration, the scope those exact packages, and a guarded import is indented rather than at
  column 0, so it falls to the sibling install-hint rule instead.
- **Rejected:** judging heaviness. Which dependencies belong in the base set stayed prose, having no
  static signature; and a dist whose import name is unrelated to its own (`Pillow` to `PIL`) is
  deliberately unmapped, a false negative taken over a false positive.
- **Landed:** #345 (Refs #303) · pack version 1.
EOF

lines: +## 2026-07-19 · born · python pack: optional-dep discipline as skill-owned checks and residue prose (#345)
+- **Source:** missingbulb/LaughCounter, whose stdlib-only core keeps the YAMNet/TensorFlow and
+  Torch/SpeechBrain models behind `[project.optional-dependencies]` extras, imported lazily per
+  backend.
+- **Reason:** a declared-optional package imported at module top level runs at `import <pkg>` time,
+  dragging the heavy or native stack into the dependency-free core and breaking every path for
+  anyone who installed the package without that extra.
+- **Actor:** the growth-discover run, merged by @missingbulb (owner).
+- **Model:** claude, per the commit trailer.
+- **Mechanism:** a blocking check of the skill. `[project.optional-dependencies]` is the only place
+  a package is *declared* optional, so the repo's own `pyproject.toml` is the ground truth that
+  makes the signature false-positive-free and lets the rule convert from prose at all; the gate is
+  that declaration, the scope those exact packages, and a guarded import is indented rather than at
+  column 0, so it falls to the sibling install-hint rule instead.
+- **Rejected:** judging heaviness. Which dependencies belong in the base set stayed prose, having no
+  static signature; and a dist whose import name is unrelated to its own (`Pillow` to `PIL`) is
+  deliberately unmapped, a false negative taken over a false positive.
+- **Landed:** #345 (Refs #303) · pack version 1.

{"number":356,"title":"Bring the canon into the conversation lifecycle; make conversation-extract a fleet run_daily task","body":"## What

Two coupled changes that put the canon home repo on the same conversation lifecycle as every other repo, and fix how extraction is delivered:

1. **Declare `grow_with_claudinite` on the canon** (`.claudinite-checks.json`, `retention_days: 10`). It's `seededByDefault` — landing on every new repo (`--init`) and every existing member (seed migration + baselining) — but baselining hard-skips the home repo (`if (signals.isHome) return {run:false}`), so the canon's hand-curated declaration predated the pack and its own sessions were outside the lifecycle. Capture is gated on the declaration, so it was silently skipped here.

2. **Make `conversation-extract` a fleet `run_daily` task, not a per-repo routine.** It was built as a separate per-repo scheduled routine on the premise that it "needs local git in the repo's own context." That was wrong: like `growth-extract`, extraction only *reads* the already-pushed logs, so it runs centrally and MCP-native (`get_file_contents` on the `conversation-logs` branch, `push_files` for lessons, `add_issue_comment` for dialogue, `delete_file` for the retention prune). Only *capture* needs the live session transcript, so capture stays in-session at merge; extraction does not.
   - New `run_daily/conversation-extract.mjs` on `grow_with_claudinite`, gating on `substantiveChange` (a real merge is when a fresh log lands — the `[skip ci]` capture commit is excluded, so it tracks the merge, not the capture) plus the weekly full sweep (which also guarantees the retention prune runs on a quiet repo). Worker `conversation-extract.md` rewritten MCP-native and central.
   - Dropped the `nightly` adoption question and all per-repo-schedule framing across the pack, README, merge-to-main, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, and the fleet routine.

3. **Add the canon's own local pack** `.claudinite/local_packs/claudinite/` as the home for Claudinite's *non-portable* lessons. The growth/conversation extract tasks write the canon's own lessons there; portable ones still become `packs/` PRs. Declared in `.claudinite-checks.json`; discovered because the canon's runner passes `localRoot`.

## Not done, and why

`canon-curation` stays in `packs/`. Its contribution is planner-dispatched `run_daily` tasks (promote, prose-to-checks-sweep), discovered via canon-only `loadPacks()`; local-pack `run_daily` is the experimental, disabled path, so relocating it to `local_packs` would silently stop those stages. Its home-only status is already encoded by `detect: null` + the home-only declaration.

## Test plan

- `routines/fleet/fleet.test.mjs` — new gate test: `conversation-extract` fires on `substantiveChange` and the weekly full sweep, quiet otherwise, and a `[skip ci]`/bot main-move alone does not trigger it.
- Confirmed the `claudinite` local pack is discovered + active and the task is registered on the pack.
- `node checks/run.mjs --all` clean; full suite 453/453.

Closes #355
Closes #357

{"number":538,"title":"Claudinite growth: conversation extract","body":"Daily `grow_with_claudinite/conversation-extract` run (dispatched by #532), slot `d2026-07-29`.

Fresh pass over the 16 logs captured 2026-07-28 on `conversation-logs` — the ones landed since the previous run, which covered through `2026-07-27T1840Z`. Three lessons cleared the bar; all land as terse prose in the home's own local pack, the only file this PR touches.

| Lesson | Source capture | Worked issue |
|---|---|---|
| The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet aggregation is Sheepdog's domain | `2026-07-28T1714Z` | #520 |
| A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's config | `2026-07-28T2200Z` | #528 |
| `subscribe_pr_activity` blocks for minutes — subscribe once, never to "wait for CI" | `2026-07-28T2208Z` | #520 |

The first two are owner corrections stated in so many words; the third is the run's measured wall-time finding — 558s of that session's 841s of total tool wall-clock (66%) was idle time bought by two duplicate subscriptions on the same PR plus a `send_later` check-in.

None became a check: the first two are judgment boundaries with no deterministic predicate, and the third is about an MCP tool's cost, not repo state. The Sheepdog one names its own drift-guard shape (no repo list in canon code) for a later pass.

**Retention prune: skipped.** `retention_days` is now unset for `grow_with_claudinite` — #527 removed the adoption question and the materialized answer — so per the task spec the prune does not run and no log was deleted. `conversation-logs` was not modified.

{"number":540,"title":"prose-to-checks: the home declares every seededByDefault pack (home-seeded-packs-declared)","body":"One conversion from the daily `prose-to-checks-sweep` (Refs #534), swept over the configured pack paths `.claudinite/local/packs` and `packs`.

## The prose that converted

`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` — *"Baselining backfill skips the home"* named its own drift-guard as future work:

> The natural drift-guard (a future check, once the home is clean) is: the home declares every `seededByDefault` non-local pack.

It passes the check-the-world test: the invariant is a comparison of two static artifacts — the `seededByDefault` flags in `packs/*/pack.mjs` against the `packs` array in `.claudinite-checks.json`. The precondition the prose set ("once the home is clean") holds today: the seeded packs are `basics`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `tidy-repo`, and all three are declared, so the rule ships at zero findings.

## The check

`home-seeded-packs-declared` (blocking, world scope) in the `claudinite` local pack.

- **Parsed, not grepped.** `git grep seededByDefault` also hits the prose *about* seeding and the engine code that reads the flag. The rule scans exactly the pack modules in the home's own `packs/` tree, with comments blanked out by a small string-aware scanner first — so a `pack.mjs` that merely mentions the flag in a comment is not mistaken for one that sets it.
- **Self-skips** where it has nothing to say: no `packs/*/pack.mjs` in the tracked tree (a consumer's canon lives under `.claudinite/shared/`), or no settings file. Local packs are out of scope by construction — they are hand-declared, never seeded.
- **Escape hatch** named in the fix line: an acceptance with a reason, if the home ever deliberately opts out of a seeded pack.

## See-it-fail

Six fixtures. The violating-input fixture — three seeded packs, one declared — was stubbed to detect nothing and **failed**, then passed once detection was written; it asserts both undeclared packs are reported (not just the first) and pins each finding's shape: rule id, `.claudinite-checks.json` anchor, blocking severity. The five quiet cases: clean, comment-only, entry-object declaration, local pack, and no-`packs/`-tree.

> Revised after review: a second violating fixture covering the single-offender case was folded into this one. It proved detection the multi-offender fixture already proves with a larger input; its unique assertions (the finding's shape) moved across and now run against every finding rather than only the first, so the trim costs no coverage.

## Prose trim

The enforced sentence is gone; the rationale stays (baselining is gated `!isHome`, so the home never receives a seeded pack automatically). The adjacent `git-github` bullet's back-reference to "the seed-based drift-guard above" is reworded to stay coherent — no rule text beyond the converted one was touched.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **897 tests, 0 failures**
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**, 8 advisory (all pre-existing `file-placement` findings under `engine/scheduler/`, none on the changed files)

Surface: the rule module, its fixture, one `pack.mjs` line, and the trimmed prose.

{"number":560,"title":"Commit-separation rule, and the three defects the deletion-test sweep surfaced","body":"Refs #563, #551. Follow-up to #552.

Originally one commit carrying four unrelated fixes. The owner's correction — unrelated concerns in one PR get one commit each — is now both the rule at the head of this branch and the shape of the branch itself. **Five commits, one concern each, each green standalone.**

## `e2b4629` — the rule

Lands in `git-github-advanced`'s "Commit often, in layers", which already owns commit layering.

**Ladder triage:** a platform setting, a PreToolUse hook, and a post-hoc check would each have to judge whether two edits belong to the same task — meaning, not signature. `feature-requirements-first` can verify an *ordering* because both its ends are identifiable artifacts (a named spec file vs code files); "these two edits are unrelated" has no such tell, and a check guessing at it would fire on every legitimately broad change. Rung 4.

**The corpus did not already carry it** (the prose-landing precondition). The two rules beside it layer a *single* task's work — failing test before implementation, docs as their own commit after. The `prose-to-checks` Bounds and the growth tasks' "don't improve unrelated rules while you're in there" scope what a run may *touch*; neither says anything about committing work that legitimately does land together. The new rule names itself as the general case the other two are instances of.

## `10bea86` — `claudinite-isolation` gave a remedy consumers can't act on

A rendered finding carries `what`/`why`/`fix`/`doc` and **never** the rule's `description` — which is where the real remedy ("inline what you need") lived. What a consumer saw was the barrier engine's default opener: *"route shared code through a shared/contracts folder both sides may use."* That's written for a two-sided edge between folders a project owns. This edge is one-sided: no shared folder exists, and the vendored canon isn't theirs to restructure.

Fixed with `crossingRemedy`, the same override seam `crossingExcuse` already used for the other half of the same `fix` string. The existing test asserted `what` and `severity` but never `fix` — which is how it survived. It does now.

## `521614b` — `skill-no-enforcement-narration` was matching zero files

It scanned `^skills/<name>/SKILL.md$`, the pre-#385 layout. Skills have lived inside their owning pack since, so the pattern matched nothing in any tree.

Its fixtures spelled the same dead layout — five green tests over a scan with no inputs. That is what let the `adopt-pack` narration paragraph sit unflagged until a human read it in #552. Now anchored on `(^|/)packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md$`, spanning `packs/` and local packs. **21 skills in scope, up from 0.** Fixtures rewritten to the real layout, plus a local-pack case and a negative for a mounted `.claude/skills/` copy.

## `273d063` — the corpus tally was hand-maintained and had drifted

`packs/README.md` claimed **41** checks against a real **65**; the paragraph beneath said **39**. The table disagreed with its own prose, and `1 : 4` / "~20% mechanized" were wrong by about a third.

Not re-typed — derived. `packRules()` becomes the one place the three rule sources are summed, `--list` prints it, and `packs-tests/catalog-tally.test.mjs` fails when the README disagrees. The hand-written per-pack breakdown is deleted; that's the part that drifted. Prose figures have no derivable source, so they're marked as the conversion audit's dated estimates. Restated: **65 : ~150 ≈ 1 : 2.3**, ~30% mechanized.

## `728df24` — the `pack-independence` remedy named a directory that doesn't exist

Same defect class as `10bea86`: agent-facing text pointing where the code isn't. It said `engine/checks_helpers` in the finding's `why` and `checks/lib` in its doc pointer, the vendor writer's fix text, and two design records. It's `engine/checks/helpers`. A grep for both stale spellings now returns nothing.

## Verification

- Full suite at HEAD: **937 pass, 0 fail** (up from 933).
- **Each of the five commits, checked out standalone in a worktree: tests green and `check_the_world` at 0 blocking, 8 advisory** — the bisectability the new rule claims, verified rather than asserted.
- The split is lossless: the tree at HEAD differs from the original bundled commit by exactly the one file the rule was added to.

{"number":595,"title":"Prove a canon change is safe for consumers: self-test, rehearsal, canary, and the rule","body":"All five phases of #593, one per commit for review.

**The gap:** canon CI proves the canon is healthy, which is not evidence about consumers — the canon's own packs are always already migrated, so a change that breaks every member passes it green. #555 did exactly that.

## The commits

| # | commit | phase |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engine: a startup self-test — can Claudinite run here?` | 1 |
| 2 | `baselining: rehearsal mode — converge against a canon branch, stamp nothing` | 0 |
| 3 | `packs-tests: the baselining rehearsal — the gate #555 needed` | 2 |
| 4 | `claudinite: enforce the consumer-safe-change rule over the canon's own diff` | 4 |
| 5 | `canary: a live rehearsal against a real repo, and the procedure doc` | 3 |

### 1 — the self-test (`engine/selftest.mjs`)

Seven probes asking *can Claudinite run here?*, not *is this repo conformant*. Each traces to a real fleet-wide failure: `pack-manifests` (#555), `hook-targets` (#397), `stamp` (#518), `skill-links` (#424). Runs at SessionStart (report-only — `--strict` there would make Claude Code discard the hook's stdout) and in baselining preprocessing, where a failure now escalates to the agent. **Mutation-tested**: neutering the stamp probe and the hook-target probe each turn the suite red.

### 2 — rehearsal mode (`CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF`)

Lets a run converge against a canon **branch**. A rehearsal stamps **nothing** — a branch head is not on trunk, and stamping it leaves the member `ref-not-on-trunk`, which the #328 anti-rewind guard then refuses to converge over. Not hypothetical: that happened by hand to all thirteen members on 2026-07-30.

### 3 — the fixture rehearsal (`packs-tests/rehearsal/`)

Four fixture consumers × two modes, converged with the **real** scripts, then self-test and sweep. `stale` mode pins the stamp in the past so migration *selection* actually fires — that is the "with a migration" half.

**Verified by reproducing #555 faithfully** — schema gains a required field *and the same commit updates every canon pack*, as actually happened:

```
canon CI       0 blocking   ← green, exactly as it was on 2026-07-29
the rehearsal  FAILS        ← naming the consumer pack that no longer validates
```

A first draft of this passed while testing nothing: the sweep inherited the canon's cwd and reported on the canon. Fixed — each fixture runs as its own git repo with itself as cwd.

### 4 — `consumer-safe-change`

A work-scoped check over the canon's own diff. Touching the manifest vocabulary, a blocking rule's severity, or the scheduler stub requires **either** a migration record **or** a rehearsal fixture. Deliberately narrow: a rule that cried wolf on every commit gets turned off, and is then worth nothing on the day it matters.

### 5 — the canary + the procedure

`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml` converges a **dedicated disposable repo** against a canon ref — manual dispatch plus automatic on merge to `main`. It runs the *canary's own vendored worker*, since that is the copy a member runs. Inert with a warning until `CLAUDINITE_CANARY_REPO` names a repo.

`consumer-safe-changes.md` gains the three-layer procedure.

## Verification

**1079 tests pass, 0 blocking**, both scopes clean. (Late in the session this environment's signing helper exhausted its file descriptors, which fails any test that commits — including nine pre-existing `github-actions` fixtures. Unrelated to this change, but it exposed a real fragility, so commit 5 also makes the rehearsal fixtures independent of the host's signing config. The final commit is unsigned for the same reason.)

## Needs you

The canary repo does not exist yet — create a disposable repo, adopt Claudinite in it, and set the repository variable `CLAUDINITE_CANARY_REPO`. Until then phase 3 is inert and the fixture rehearsal is the only consumer gate.

Closes #593. {"number":661,"title":"Move engineering-practices from a skill into basics/RULES.md","body":"`engineering-practices` loaded **once in 82 captured sessions** (2026-07-19 → 2026-08-05, from this repo's `usage.GENERATED.json` fold) despite describing itself as "use before writing or editing code". The trigger wasn't the thing to fix — content that applies to every code change shouldn't be gated behind an on-demand load. `inject-pack-prose.mjs` emits every declared pack's `RULES.md` at SessionStart, so the content now loads in every session in every member.

**The move.** The 26 bullets become an "Engineering practices" section in `packs/basics/RULES.md`; `packs/basics/skills/engineering-practices/` is deleted and dropped from the `skills` list in `pack.mjs`. Relative links in the transplanted text are rebased from the skill directory to `packs/basics/`.

**References repointed.** The three rules whose `doc` field named the skill — `shared-constants`, `generated-merge-driver`, `node/earn-each-dependency` — now point at `packs/basics/RULES.md`, matching the convention that non-skill docs carry a repo path. The cross-references in `bug-investigation`, `repo-text-sweeps`, `writing-tests` and `git-github-advanced` follow, as does the section heading in `docs/conversion-inventory.md`.

**One content edit.** `pack-no-enforcement-narration` fired on the single-source-of-truth bullet — legal inside a skill, blocking in pack prose — because it narrated what the `shared-constants` check does on failure. The account of the check is gone; the instruction it carried (declare the entry, keep the value on one line, use `regex: true` for values that move) stands on its own.

Full unit suite (1167 tests) and `check_the_world.mjs` green — 0 blocking.

Closes #660

{"number":746,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Daily growth-extract for slot `d2026-08-11`, dispatched by #743. Three lessons, all prose, in the repo's own local packs. No shared canon touched.

## Activity half — `013dce0`, `952d21b`; merged #741, #707; touched #740, #410, #492, #739

Neither merged PR carried review discussion. The window's argued verdicts are in **#740**'s owner-review round, which yields one keeper:

- **`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/item-routing.md`** → *Dedupe against the whole corpus*: **sweep last, and case-insensitively.** #740's similarity sweep ran *before* two lessons were re-homed out of a folded-away skill file into `packs/basics/RULES.md`, so **three** copies of the unknown-state rule reached the owner, who found them by reading; the re-run then caught a further capitalised pair the case-sensitive pattern had missed. The section said what to dedupe *against* and nothing about *when in the change* to do it.

Only `2026-08-10T0651Z--issue-708` carries human dialogue; the other five are unattended executor runs with no friction signal. Both keepers land in **`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`**:

- **Standing owner decision** — *a code deprecation rides the standard `@deprecated` tag, never a bespoke conformance check* (owner ruling 2026-08-09, #707). `deprecated-session-scope` was authored as a `basics` check and deleted the same day it was reviewed. {"number":776,"title":"Versioned updates Phase 1: define the engine release","body":"Phase 1's first box of #768, plus two defects Phase 0's relocation left behind.

## The release definition

**A release is the commit that bumps `ENGINE_VERSION`, legitimate only once the live canary rehearsal has passed against the tree being released** (your decision, 2026-08-12). No tag and no separate artifact: the updater clones `main` at its newest bumped ref, so the version lives in the file the mount already carries and there is nothing to cut, push or forget.

[`engine/RELEASES.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/claudinite-issue-768-g2qga2/engine/RELEASES.md) is the log and the procedure — dispatch the canary against your branch, wait for it, bump and add the row citing that run, merge. Version 1's row cites the real post-merge run against `8dbb096` ([run 31628529342](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31628529342), green), and says plainly that it was post-merge because the procedure landed after it.

`engine-release-record` (canon-local, work scope, blocking) is what makes it hold. The canary runs in *another repository*, so no check can verify the run happened — but a check can insist the claim is made where a later reader looks, with the run id that settles it. It fires on a bump with no row, a row citing no run, and a version that moves backwards. Editing `version.mjs` without moving the number stays an ordinary engine edit, so the release toll is paid only by releases.

Its last test is a live-selection assertion: the real `RELEASES.md` must answer for the real `ENGINE_VERSION`. A fixture would keep proving the matching works while the shipping version quietly had no row — the #560 shape.

## Two defects from the Phase 0 relocation

- **`consumer-safe-change` no longer recognised a migration record.** Its path pattern still spelled the flat `migrations/` directory the records left in #769, so it matched nothing any branch could produce and the one escape hatch it offers — ship a record — had silently stopped counting. Both homes count now. Watched the new assertion fail against the old pattern before fixing it.
- **It fired on canon-only rules.** A rule under `.claudinite/local/packs/` reaches no consumer by construction (the vendor set carries `engine/` and `packs/`, never that tree), so demanding a migration record for one is a toll on every canon-only rule — including this PR's own. Narrowed; the same module under a shipped pack still counts.

## Consumer safety

Additive, and nothing here ships to a member: `engine/RELEASES.md` is engine `.md` (maintainer reference, excluded from the vendor set by the blanket rule — it is not on the operational whitelist), and the new rule lives in the canon's own local pack. No migration record and no rehearsal fixture is the honest answer, which is exactly the narrowing above.

{"number":944,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth-extract capture over the window bound in #943 — both source halves in one run, one commit, one PR, per [task.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-extract/task.md).

## Activity half
Read: 16 window commits, 15 merged PRs (diff + review discussion), 3 touched PRs, 14 touched issues. Four parallel research passes, deduped against the existing corpus.

## Conversation half
Read: 18 conversation-log captures since the last pass (issues #864–#931). Three parallel research passes, deduped against the existing corpus.

## What landed — `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`

One correction and twelve additions, mostly folded into existing bullets that already owned the territory:

- **Correction**: the "Waiting for something to happen" rule pointed at `Monitor` for a run's status — but for GitHub CI/PR checks specifically, `Monitor` and `curl` are proxy-blind here (`api.github.com` is blocked) and silently report "still running" until timeout. Measured ~26 min lost across two PRs (#880). Now carved out with the correct read-the-check-runs approach.
- Simulator-building must model the engine's actual artifact, not the rule's stated intent — the root cause of an episode-boundary livelock that stayed invisible until the sim was corrected (#925).
- A retry test for identity-arbitrated state (a claim, a lock) must come from a **different actor**, not just a second call — a same-actor retry can't expose the identity-masked race that hid a bug until two executors raced (#925).
- Retiring or reshaping a protocol the engine exposes needs a sweep for **cross-repo** callers — a `FORCE_TASKS` migration broke Sheepdog's only caller because the sweep never left this repo (#929, #801, #907).
- Generated content written into a GitHub issue/PR body needs an explicit byte budget in two tiers — `growth-dedup`'s own brief once rendered 350KB against the 64KB cap.
- Standing owner decision recorded: `.claudinite-checks.json` config validation is a JSON Schema, never a bespoke vocabulary (built and reverted, #919).
- Re-verifying a branch against a moved `main`: rebase, never merge (a merge commit trips the squash-merge-history gate) — paid twice in one evening (#880).
- After a squash-merge, `git remote prune origin` before touching that branch again, or the next push is rejected on a stale ref (#922).
- Restore a deliberate see-it-fail mutation via `git checkout`/`stash`, never a `.bak` taken before later edits (#922).
- Capture one test-suite run to a file and grep it — don't re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice the same output (5 reruns cost 4.5 min, #930/#931).
- Whitelist tests for the vendor set should assert the whole containing directory, not just the one file that broke (#907).
- Answer every claim in an owner comment in the first reply, including the one you push back on — a silently-dropped claim costs a round-trip later (#864).
- Converge an unattended run's outcome label/comment/close as the very next action once known, never deferred to end-of-session recall — two runs closed `outcome:done` with their own PR still open needing a human (#939, #892).

## Upgrade pass
Ran prose-to-checks over this run's own additions: none clear a confident, narrow static signature (they're session-judgment and workflow-discipline rules, not repo-state patterns) — all thirteen land as prose per the "can't be made confident → prose, never a broken check" rule.

## Retention prune
Not due — `retention_days` unset for this repo (capture-only adoption). Nothing deleted.

## Tests
`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 1893/1893 pass.

{"number":962,"title":"Force fleet delivery only where member variation can break it","body":"Closes #961.

The standing rule read as unconditional — and every canon change touches what members receive, so taken literally it forces the fleet for a doc edit or a file move (the case that prompted this: #956 moved a pasted-by-hand script between folders).

The gate is now the question itself: force in-session only when **"will it work on every repo?"** has an answer that depends on how members *differ* — engine flow, a contract their own files must satisfy, a stub or workflow, a migration record, a new config key. The how (Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, report per member unasked, attach the repos verification needs, 204 means queued) is unchanged and still attached to that case. Where the change is uniform by construction, the nightly converge *is* the delivery.

Prose rung, per the promotion ladder: the rule is an in-flight judgment call, so no check can carry it. The prose-rung equivalent of see-it-fail is showing the corpus doesn't already cover it — `packs/sheepdog/RULES.md` documents only *how* to press the lever, and nothing anywhere states *when*.

{"number":979,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth-extract run for #978.

**Activity half**: 16 window commits, 15 merged PRs read whole (diff + review discussion), 3 touched PRs, 12 touched issues.
**Conversation half**: fresh pass over 13 captures since the last run (issues #939–#974).
**Retention prune**: not due (`retention_days` unset for this repo — capture-only adoption).

Landed 13 additions and one refinement in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`:

- After any scheduler-mechanism flip, re-audit every `frequency: 'manual'` task's precondition (#929, #921, #971)
- A diff-scoped CI check needs an explicit base fetch + non-empty-scope hard-fail, and a wiring/guard test must assert the runner *answers*, never that *this branch* passes (#966, #970)
- A rename sweep recomputes golden values from the live function and never renames a dated historical record documenting what existed before (#957)
- `.github/workflows/` files can only arrive seeded at adoption — the nightly update's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused there (#935)
- A vocabulary the engine enforces immediately but packs adopt only on version bump can self-block its own fix, invisibly (#938)
- Classify setup-time state by persistence scope before choosing its mechanism; a capability belongs in the pack owning its runtime surface (#956)
- A uniform signal across the whole fleet right after a shared mechanism changes needs a timing check before it reads as "frozen" (#801, #939)
- A dropped dispatch parameter must fail loudly — a silently-dead safety knob defaults to the most dangerous mode (#974, owner-authored)
- Cross-pack shared logic never lands in `engine/`; prefer per-pack duplication over a shared drift-guarded module (#959)
- Decide a new capability's distribution model (local tool / engine / opt-in pack) before writing its first file (#934)
- A canon pack's `RULES.md` edit needs its `README.md` rule-index row updated in the same change — only the dedicated test catches the drift, not `check_the_world.mjs` (#870)
- A scratch probe commit made with `commit -am` can swallow and then destroy unrelated pending edits (#939)
- Refined "Waiting for something to happen": poll check-runs with backoff, don't dual-poll alongside a running watcher, and dispatch `workflow_dispatch` after a bot-authored push (#958, #960, #974)
- New: hyperlink human hand-off steps to the deepest settings URL, never list a no-op default step (#952, owner-authored)

**Upgrade pass (prose-to-checks)**: none of the 14 items convert — all are session-judgment, architectural, or workflow-discipline rules with no confident static signature to scan for. Stays prose.

Full test suite green (2100/2100).

The read operation to perform on a single issue.

1. get - Get issue details. method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.

{"number":1006,"title":"Shim the engine paths fielded pack copies still import","body":"Closes #1004.

Forcing Shepherd's converge immediately after #993 merged found this — which is exactly what that force is for. The run went **green** and the stamp **did not move**: [run 32147342762](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32147342762), PR missingbulb/Shepherd#45 open and `needs-human`.

```
pack-manifests: the pack in packs/core failed to load:
  Cannot find module '.../engine/scheduler/slots.mjs'
  imported from '.../packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs'
```

## The window nothing closes

The converged tree carried the **new engine** beside the **old `core` pack**. That is not a race — the engine lane and the pack lane are separate PRs on separate cycles, and pack delivery is version-gated per pack, so **every member spends a window holding the new engine and an old pack.**

A `packs/` file importing an `engine/` module is therefore a stale caller of an instantly-current engine. This repo already has the rule for the other lane — *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it"* — and this is the same asymmetry one lane over.

It is worse than a broken task: a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test, so the converge **refuses to land at all**, and the member cannot receive the pack version that would have fixed it. Self-healing is exactly what it takes away.

#974's precondition asked the right question of the wrong callers: *"deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does."* True — three **pack files** import it.

## The fix

`slots.mjs` and `run.mjs` return as thin shims over `calendar.mjs` and `github.mjs`, carrying only what a fielded pack version imports, with the retirement condition stated at the definition (read members' stamped `packVersions`; don't guess a release).

`parseOverrides` is the one body that cannot re-export — its home is now a **pack**, and the engine may not import a pack. So it is duplicated, and the drift guard runs both copies over the same inputs rather than comparing text. Where they legitimately differ (the pack's parser ignores prose, because a work item's Context is prose first), the test asserts the difference instead of hiding it.

## The guard

`engine-tests/scheduler/engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` derives which imports are fielded by walking the pack tree's history, so it needs no hand-kept list. Two things it learned the hard way, both pinned:

- **The trunk, not `--all`.** An import that only existed on an unmerged branch is not fielded. Scanning every ref fires on whatever is in flight — which it did on its first run, against #941's branch.
- **It refuses a shallow checkout.** With no history the scan finds nothing and reports clean — a green run proving nothing. CI uses `fetch-depth: 0`; the test now asserts that rather than assuming it.

Watched failing before green: removing either shim turns it red with the module named.

## Verification

2072 tests pass; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The lesson is in the canon's local pack, beside the `updates/*` rule it generalizes.

Shepherd re-converges once this lands, which supersedes its #45 — and only then is #974's outstanding `fleet-baseline` `DRY_RUN` meaningful, since Shepherd's vendored worker still reads the old channel until it converges.

{"number":1015,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Refs #1014 — the `growth-extract` daily capture over the 2026-08-18 window. Six lessons, all into `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`; nothing else touched.

## Activity half — three

- **The see-it-fail restore rule was incomplete, and #1010 said so.** Its last comment flagged it as an open, unlanded lesson (*"raised here so it isn't lost"*): the rule says restore with `git checkout -- <file>` at the moment of mutating, but never says the file must already be committed. `git checkout --` restores from the index, so it destroys uncommitted work in that same file just as thoroughly as the `.bak` the rule already bans — which happened once in that session. Refined in place beside the existing text rather than appended.
- **A named knob the corpus mentions is not evidence it exists.** One window carried all three misses, which is why this is a rule and not an anecdote: designed-and-never-built (`CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL`) beside retired-with-its-mechanism (`exclusive`), both documented as live (#975); a writer whose last reader went, with nothing saying so (`session_scope`, #993); and a **reader whose writer went** — the usage fold's `tasks` census, whose parser outlived the log lines it read, so the rows keep counting plausibly until Actions retention ages out and then count nothing (#994). The rule names that third shape as the one to design against: deleting a writer is the same change as marking its series historical.
- **A rename whose word is also stored data is not finished at the code** (#1013). The usage aggregate holds rows keyed by the old spelling, so the decode side must rename them or the next encode writes those historical counts as `null` — silently, and only for the old rows. Plus: on a *second* rename of one name, map every legacy spelling straight to today's rather than chaining.

## Conversation half — three, from the fresh window's captures

- **Measured: re-running the whole suite and `check_the_world` per edit of a many-file sweep is what the session costs.** Of one night's tool wall-clock, the session that landed #993 spent 18 full-suite runs (18 min) and 22 world sweeps (7 min) out of 26 min; #941's spent 22 (22 min) and 27 (12 min) out of 33 min; #992's 7 and 8 out of 14 min. Both are whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file of a sweep. The existing rule covers only re-running to *re-slice* unchanged output; this covers re-running while iterating.
- **A conversation-scope check must screen the harness's plain-text pseudo-turns, not only the tag-wrapped ones.** `humanText` in `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs` drops a user entry starting with `<`, which lets a bracketed marker straight through — `comment-classification` blocked a session on `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]` as *"the owner's latest comment"*. Landed as a rule naming that call site; a fix there is its own change.
- **An owner ruling on surfaced numbers** (#1001): no monotonic cumulative total, no figure nothing measures, a window against the previous window — and a field that cannot be had from the reads already being made is named **absent** rather than approximated.

## Deliberately not landed

- The `claudinite-` pack-prefix ruling from #1010 is **already on #1011's branch** as an edit to this same file. Landing it here would collide with the PR that owns it.
- The advisory-then-blocking staging of a fleet conformance rule (#991) reads as adjacent to `consumer-safe-changes.md` and the existing member-contract rule; left out rather than duplicated.

## The prose-to-checks upgrade pass converted none of the six

Scope was this run's own additions only. Each is in-flight process (a restore step, a tool-call sequence) or judgment with no static signature; the two that have a signature would only pin today's code — the bar's first rejected shape. The #1001 rule also cleared the working-rule gate rather than reading as a product statement: it is true whatever any one surface decides to show.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2095 tests, 2094 pass. The one failure is `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` refusing a **shallow checkout** (its own #1006 self-guard, `"too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history"`); re-run after `git fetch --depth=300` it is 3/3 green, and CI checks out at `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `check_the_work` exit 0. `check_the_world`: **0 blocking, 57 advisory** — the same count #1013 measured against `main`, so this change adds no finding.
- `growth-write-scope` gate: OK, every touched path under the local packs.
- All 44 added lines are ≤ 100 bytes (`rules-line-length`); the four over-limit lines still in the file predate this change (#766).

{"number":2214,"title":"Usage review: skills declare their expected usage, rules read it back","body":"Implements [docs/usage-review/DESIGN.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/usage-review/DESIGN.md) — the loop that reads back whether a placement on the promotion ladder held. Advances #2084.

Every skill declares how it expects to be *reached*; the fold records what happened; a file of readable rule declarations compares the two; and a weekly owner-gated triage turns a finding that has lasted into a proposed diff. **Nothing in the loop merges on its own**, so a rule that turns out to be wrong costs a declined pull request and leaves no trace.

## A skill declares its mechanism, never its rate

The first draft had a skill predict its own frequency (`loads-per-sessions: 1 in 20`). That is a guess the record can never contradict, so the rule dividing by it measured its author rather than the skill. Both are gone, and with the rate went the distinction between `routine` and `rare` — two spellings of one state, which `choosing-declared-field` forbids. The vocabulary is three mechanisms:

| `expect` | claims | the record contradicts it by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adoption` | loaded while its pack is being adopted | zero loads inside the declaration window |
| `triggered` | loaded by its own force-load declarations | loads far under the moments those declarations named |
| `judgment` | loaded when the model judges the description fits | nothing — only *always loaded* applies |

64 skills: **37 `triggered`, 24 `judgment`, 3 `adoption`**, none unstated. The check refuses the one half a file can prove wrong by itself — `triggered` with no force-load declaration — and refuses a retired key left in the block rather than ignoring it.

## What it found on this repo's real record

Run end to end against the 28 days to 2026-09-20: **52 findings, 528 pairs not evaluated**. Almost every "not evaluated" is a counter this branch adds that no fold has written yet, which reads as *not recorded* rather than as zero — the boundary working as designed.

The counters over the last 25 captured sessions already show the loop's point:

- `searching-for-a-tool` loaded 11 times and a guard held the call **every one of them** — `skill-forced-only-small`'s exact signature.
- `fetching-from-the-web`'s result trigger fired 3 times and was followed **none** — `trigger-fires-unfollowed`.
- The Stop sweep's timing record, first run: `squash-merge-history` at 928ms of 1175ms total.

## Scope decisions taken

- **The fold stays in `claudinite-tasks`.** Its file is the dashboard's past-data plane, so it is not growth-only and the "move it if only growth uses it" condition is not met.
- **16 rules, implemented as §3 writes them** — the seventeenth was the one reading the retired rate. Most findings are `check-never-fires`, above the design's own "more than twelve means tight" line. That is the threshold as specified; the retrospective is where it gets re-judged, and each rule's provenance file already carries the reasoning to judge it against.
- **The prose-twin definition sees 2 twins in 95 checks.** Narrow by design; the review reports `twinless` so a reader weighs the definition rather than trusting a number that hid it.

## Three gaps fixed at their cause

Each was exposed by this work and would have blocked the next person the same way:

- `task-declaration-shape` read `needsItem` but not `takesArg`, so **no** task-local precondition term could ever take an argument.
- `provenance-change-recorded` read a declared `usage` block as a decision owing an entry — 63 entries recording that a declaration was written.
- The rehearsal's `canon-home` fixture carried no skill, so the shelf it models never exercised the skill rules the curation pack polices.

## Still unproven

No scheduled run has opened the review's pull request, filed an issue or closed one — that needs `main`. A `verify-in-production` issue follows the merge, and the design doc goes when it reads back true.

## Checks

Rebased onto `main`; the two conflicts were append-only provenance files whose full history `main` backfilled while this branch held the shallow-clone placeholder, so `main`'s entries stand and this branch's append after them. Full suite 3749/3749 (48 test declarations more than `main`). `check_the_world` 0 blocking. `check_the_work` 0 blocking, no findings.

Automerge: `nothing`.

{"number":2214,"title":"Usage review: skills declare their expected usage, rules read it back","body":"Implements [docs/usage-review/DESIGN.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/usage-review/DESIGN.md) — the loop that reads back whether a placement on the promotion ladder held. Advances #2084.

Every skill declares how it expects to be *reached*; the fold records what happened; a file of readable rule declarations compares the two; and a weekly owner-gated triage turns a finding that has lasted into a proposed diff. **Nothing in the loop merges on its own**, so a rule that turns out to be wrong costs a declined pull request and leaves no trace.

## A skill declares its mechanism, never its rate

The first draft had a skill predict its own frequency (`loads-per-sessions: 1 in 20`). That is a guess the record can never contradict, so the rule dividing by it measured its author rather than the skill. Both are gone, and with the rate went the distinction between `routine` and `rare` — two spellings of one state, which `choosing-declared-field` forbids. The vocabulary is three mechanisms:

| `expect` | claims | the record contradicts it by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adoption` | loaded while its pack is being adopted | zero loads inside the declaration window |
| `triggered` | loaded by its own force-load declarations | loads far under the moments those declarations named |
| `judgment` | loaded when the model judges the description fits | nothing — only *always loaded* applies |

64 skills: **37 `triggered`, 24 `judgment`, 3 `adoption`**, none unstated. The check refuses the one half a file can prove wrong by itself — `triggered` with no force-load declaration — and refuses a retired key left in the block rather than ignoring it.

## What it found on this repo's real record

Run end to end against the 28 days to 2026-09-20: **52 findings, 528 pairs not evaluated**. Almost every "not evaluated" is a counter this branch adds that no fold has written yet, which reads as *not recorded* rather than as zero — the boundary working as designed.

The counters over the last 25 captured sessions already show the loop's point:

- `searching-for-a-tool` loaded 11 times and a guard held the call **every one of them** — `skill-forced-only-small`'s exact signature.
- `fetching-from-the-web`'s result trigger fired 3 times and was followed **none** — `trigger-fires-unfollowed`.
- The Stop sweep's timing record, first run: `squash-merge-history` at 928ms of 1175ms total.

## Scope decisions taken

- **The fold stays in `claudinite-tasks`.** Its file is the dashboard's past-data plane, so it is not growth-only and the "move it if only growth uses it" condition is not met.
- **16 rules, implemented as §3 writes them** — the seventeenth was the one reading the retired rate. Most findings are `check-never-fires`, above the design's own "more than twelve means tight" line. That is the threshold as specified; the retrospective is where it gets re-judged, and each rule's provenance file already carries the reasoning to judge it against.
- **The prose-twin definition sees 2 twins in 95 checks.** Narrow by design; the review reports `twinless` so a reader weighs the definition rather than trusting a number that hid it.

## Three gaps fixed at their cause

Each was exposed by this work and would have blocked the next person the same way:

- `task-declaration-shape` read `needsItem` but not `takesArg`, so **no** task-local precondition term could ever take an argument.
- `provenance-change-recorded` read a declared `usage` block as a decision owing an entry — 63 entries recording that a declaration was written.
- The rehearsal's `canon-home` fixture carried no skill, so the shelf it models never exercised the skill rules the curation pack polices.

## Still unproven

No scheduled run has opened the review's pull request, filed an issue or closed one — that needs `main`. A `verify-in-production` issue follows the merge, and the design doc goes when it reads back true.

## Checks

Rebased onto `main`; the two conflicts were append-only provenance files whose full history `main` backfilled while this branch held the shallow-clone placeholder, so `main`'s entries stand and this branch's append after them. Full suite 3749/3749 (48 test declarations more than `main`). `check_the_world` 0 blocking. `check_the_work` 0 blocking, no findings.

Automerge: `nothing`.

{"number":1197,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth-extract's daily capture pass over the 2026-08-22 activity window (queue item #1196).

## What was mined

- **Activity half**: the 10 substantive commits in the window, the 11 PRs merged in it (diff + review discussion — none of the 11 had any review discussion at all; each was a solo-authored, self-merged PR), the 4 touched-but-not-merged PRs, and the 16 touched issues.
- **Conversation half**: the fresh pass (13 captures from the last 24h on `origin/conversation-logs`) and the hindsight pass (6 captures from the branch's oldest 24h window).

Nearly everything found was either already covered verbatim by this pack's existing corpus, or was itself the commit/PR that had already landed the lesson directly into canon prose (`packs/basics/RULES.md`) or a check in the same window — so there was nothing left to re-capture from it locally.

## Three new lessons landed

All three are judgment-shaped (no static signature a check could observe), so each stayed prose per the promotion ladder; the prose-to-checks upgrade pass over this run's own additions confirmed none convert.

1. **Retire a `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` once the system it describes is built** — dissolve it into the module headers and pack READMEs that must independently state the same facts, keeping only what's genuinely irreplaceable (an owner-decision record with its rationale). From #1169.
2. **A same-title work-item mutex is blind to two items that conflict without sharing a title** — key a conflict guard on the target the write lands on (serialize via the queue's own `Blocked-by:` field), not on the requester's phrasing. From #1119.
3. **A "this PR bumped X" check that diffs only against `main` can misread a stacked PR's inherited bump as its own**, and skip re-bumping for that PR's own edits — re-verify after every earlier PR in the stack actually lands. From #1119 (`pack-version-bumped`).

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — green (2520/2520; one pre-existing shallow-clone environmental failure, unrelated to this change, resolved by deepening the local fetch before the run).
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 71 advisory (all pre-existing elsewhere in the tree; nothing new introduced by this change).

{"number":1290,"title":"Make the scheduler and executor workflows thin wrappers over engine code","body":"Closes #1289

## Why

`.github/workflows/` is the one vendored path a converge cannot push into — a push authored with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not write a workflow file, so a member's copy of these two files moves only through a PR a human merges, one repo at a time. Every engine module beside them converges nightly and unattended.

That makes every line of logic **or prose** in these two files a line whose change costs a fleet-wide human-merged PR. They carried ~90 lines of comment and three inline `github-script` programs.

## What moved

| New module | Was |
|---|---|
| `engine/scheduler/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs` | the scheduler's `drain` job script |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/workflow-failure.mjs` | the `report-failure` job script |
| `engine/scheduler/queue/executor-continuation.mjs` | the executor's `continue-the-chain` script |

All three reuse the engine helpers the YAML was re-implementing (`dispatchWorkflow`, `createIssue`, `ensureLabels`) — which is also how the dispatch and the create stop being judged by their response bodies rather than their status. `dispatchWorkflow` gains an optional `inputs` argument for the chain depth.

The YAML keeps only the comments a reader of the YAML alone genuinely needs: the literal label spellings the event trigger cannot decode, the stale-copy note on the drain gate, and the `# claudinite:secrets` marker the converge stamps against. Both copies of both files — the stub and the canon's own — move together.

Net on the four workflow files: **479 lines → 301**, and no program left in any of them.

## Guards

A thin wrapper names its logic by literal path, which is a new way to break a member, so three:

- **`scheduler-workflows-are-thin`** (blocking, world, canon-local pack) — refuses `actions/github-script` and a block `run:` in either stub and either canon copy. Watched on all four surfaces, not one of two (#1138).
- **A vendor-set test** — every module the stubs name is actually in the computed vendor set. Without it, dropping a module from the set produces a member whose workflow parses, starts, and dies on a missing file: a queue that silently stops draining.
- **A `thin-workflows` rehearsal shape** — `old-workflows` from the other end: that shape asks whether a member left behind still converges, this one asks whether a member that arrived does.

The rule is also recorded as prose in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` with a `VERSIONS.md` row.

## Fixed on the way

The scheduler workflow's header cited a `scheduler-stub-parity` check that exists **nowhere in the tree** — a stale `doc:`-style pointer with nothing to catch it. The real guard is the pair of drift tests in `engine-tests/scheduler/converge-wiring.test.mjs`, which the header now names.

## One accepted narrowing

The failure-escalation and continuation jobs now need `checkout` + `setup-node` to run their module, where `github-script` needed neither. If the repo checkout itself fails, those jobs cannot file their issue. The modules are import-light and a failed checkout fails every job equally and shows red, so this trades a rare unreported case for a surface that can actually be changed — but it is a real narrowing, not a wash.

## Verification

- Full suite: **2687 pass, 0 fail** (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`).
- `check_the_world`: 0 blocking. `check_the_work`: clean.
- See-it-fail run on every new assertion: the ensure-before-create ordering, the dispatch status check, the continuation cap and depth default, the vendor-set guard (with a deliberately unshipped module), and `scheduler-workflows-are-thin` against the real tree with `github-script` restored — all went red, then green.

{"number":1310,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"## Summary

Daily `growth-extract` run over both lesson sources — repo activity and captured conversation logs — Context-scoped to work item #1305.

**Activity half** (commits c14e24a/eec43a5/c0dd572/bd77c1f, merged PRs #1294/#1290/#1257/#1287, the touched PRs/issues named in the item's Context): read whole. No genuinely new lesson — the one candidate that looked promising (a dashboard import-graph pin missing a module) is already covered by the corpus's existing "generate derived data rather than hand-maintaining it" guidance, and the scheduler/executor thin-wrapper lesson from #1290 is already landed (2026-08-23, owner request).

- **Closing keyword on a queue work-item's own PR** — a session wrote `Closes #1275` on the very issue `converge-item.mjs` is supposed to park at `needs-human-approval`, self-caught before push. GitHub's native closing keyword fires on merge regardless of any converge logic, so it would have silently overridden the intended park state.
- **Re-waiting on a signal that already failed to move** — a fleet-follow wait re-waited six blind minutes hoping stragglers would catch up after a first wait already showed no movement; reading the gating logic (a minute) would have said not to expect any.
- **`git ls-files`-based test runner misses just-created, unstaged test files** — two full-suite runs came back green without ever executing the session's own new test files, because they weren't staged yet.

Everything else surfaced (the recurring `converge-item.mjs` MCP-only-session failure, ~8 independent occurrences) is already comprehensively tracked at #1149/#1133 with its own reproduction evidence; the actual fix is engine code outside this task's write scope (`.claudinite/local/packs/` only), so no rule was added for it here — landing a workaround-encoding rule would also risk canonizing a fix the owner already flagged as "not a sanctioned procedure" on #1149.

**Upgrade pass**: all three additions are about in-session temporal behavior with no static artifact signature (per the check-the-world test), so none convert to a check this run — they stay prose.

- **`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`** — three new RULES.md entries + matching VERSIONS.md rows.

{"number":1315,"title":"Cut the local pack's RULES.md to one trigger and directive per rule","body":"Closes #1312

`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` carried 63% of this repo's session rule tokens (~11,500 of ~18,300) and had grown ~900 tokens a day over the preceding week.

**8,435 → 5,359 words (37%), 114 → 154 rules.** Session rule tokens ~18,300 → ~14,000.

Two passes, one commit each.

## Pass 1 — the audit method

The `authoring-agent-docs` audit that #760 and #894 ran on `packs/basics/RULES.md`. That one worked by folding clauses back into parent rules; this file barely had that problem, since `growth-extract` already appends one situation-keyed block per lesson. What it had was **per-rule incident archaeology** — issue ids, dates, quoted owner exchanges, the story behind each rule. Removed, per the skill's own line: *"the commit that added the rule keeps them… a rule that reads as a post-mortem with a directive at the top is the wrong way round."*

Three structural changes, each verified against the tree first:

- **Split out** *Creating the artifact a check will demand* — a trailing clause of the mechanize-a-procedure rule, but a reader can arrive at it without that one.
- **Cut** *Writing check-the-work* — `basics` already carries see-it-fail as the ladder rule, and both load in the same session.
- **Cut** *Judging whether a member is fresh* — it **contradicted** `claudinite-lifecycle`, which loads beside it: the local rule said read `ref`, the canon rule rules out `ref` along with `claudinite.updated`, because the versioned flows stamp versions only. Whichever a session reached first decided the answer.
- **Stripped** *Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land* to the one diagnosis `claudinite-lifecycle` does not already carry verbatim.

## Pass 2 — one trigger, one directive

67 words/rule was still too long, because most rules carried their reasoning inline and several carried two or three situations in one block. A bundled rule cannot be trimmed without losing one of its situations, so this pass splits first, then cuts.

**113 → 154 rules, mean 35 words, median 35, longest 53.** Reasoning is out; measurements survive only where the number *is* the argument (the 81% wall-clock, the 25-of-26 minutes, the 46 truncated test files).

Representative splits: *Landing a change to what members receive* separated from *Forcing fleet delivery* (the second fires once you have already decided to); *Changing an export in `updates/*`* from its retirement condition; the scheduler-workflow rule from where to move the program.

The header now carries the budget, so appends hold the shape:

> Keep each rule near 40 words: the trigger, the directive, and a consequence clause only where the rule cannot be applied without it. Split a rule that carries two situations; the evidence it came from lives in `VERSIONS.md` and the issue, never here.

## Verification

A subject diff is meaningless across a 113 → 154 split, so coverage was checked two ways:

- **Identifiers** — every backticked identifier the old file named, matched against the new one. Twenty missing: sixteen were examples that re-expressed their rule (`ensure_ascii`, `build_vars`, `git stash`); four were load-bearing and restored — the literal `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`, `converge-item.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/session-transcript.mjs`, `pack-discovery-entry-await`.
- **Subjects** — every old rule subject matched to a new rule by shared content words. None unmatched.

`check_the_work` clean. `check_the_world` **0 blocking**, 77 advisory (unchanged), none against this pack. Full suite **2,708/2,708**. No line over 100 bytes, clearing the seven that tripped the advisory `rules-line-length`.

## Carried out separately

The `packs/* → .claudinite/local` barrier gap, which was sitting as a TODO inside a rule, is now #1313 with its four still-dangling `canon-curation` references listed.

The header budget binds sessions that read this file. Holding `growth-extract` itself to it is a change to the two extract skills in the canon — a separate PR, not done here.

{"number":1338,"title":"Drop the executor stub's comment about what not to put in it","body":"The secrets block in `packs/claudinite-tasks/stubs/claudinite-executor.yml` carried a paragraph explaining why the workflow does *not* serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an edit — #1336's reversal — rather than about the file in front of the reader, and the workflow stubs are the one surface where a comment is pure freight: every member vendors them verbatim, forever, and nothing reads them. The reason belongs where the decision is implemented, and [`converge-workflows.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq/packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs) already carries it beside the code that stamps the list.

What stays is what the block is for: what the converge writes there, and that it writes directly beneath the marker — which is why the marker is the last line.

The canon's own `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` is edited in the same commit, and the two whole files still differ only in the sanctioned places (the hand-maintained note, the hand-maintained secret list, and the repo-root `run:` paths).

## The check that fired on it

`consumer-safe-change` blocked this diff, asking for a migration record or a rehearsal fixture — for a comment deletion. A `#` opens a comment only at line start or after whitespace, so a `#` inside a scalar (`echo 'a # b'`) is still a real character, and a stub whose head or base cannot be read stays a contract surface — the fail-safe answer.

Seen to fail first: the comment-only case was red against the old rule, and the earlier `check_the_work` run reported `1 blocking` on this same diff.
