## What landed

Two lessons from this window's activity (15 commits, 21 merged PRs, 5 touched PRs, 27 touched
issues) and conversation-log pass (30 captured sessions — the fresh 24h window plus the oldest-24h
hindsight window), both landed as prose in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` under
"Working with the owner and the session's tools." Neither is a static file-content pattern a
declared check could observe, so neither clears any rung above prose on the promotion ladder.

- **A Bash call that `cd`s outside the project root gets silently reset back to it on the next
  call.** Evidenced directly in this session's own read of #1444 (`cd /home/user/claudinite && grep
  ...` succeeded, the next call's result carried "Shell cwd was reset to /home/user/Shepherd") and
  corroborated independently in #1426, #1160, #1449 and #1452 — at least 10 occurrences across 6
  sessions, each rediscovering it by trial. Provenance comment: #1444.

- **Asserting why a system behaved a certain way needs the primary evidence read first** — the
  issue's own body/comments, or the enforcing source line — not inferred from structure or memory.
  #1461 shipped a merged PR (#1462) that fixed the wrong thing before the owner's correction forced
  a read of the real evidence and a superseding PR (#1466); #1491 independently self-caught the same
  mistake shape the same day before shipping anything wrong. Provenance comments: #1461, #1491.

## What didn't land

Several other real candidates surfaced but didn't clear the two-strongest cut for this run's prose
ration (at most two new `RULES.md` rules per run), or turned out to already be covered / not yet
settled enough to state as a directive:

- A concurrent version-bump race (#1482) — two PRs bumping a pack to the identical next version
  collide silently, and the second's real content ships under a version the fleet already believes
  published. Real and owner-investigated, but the remedy is still undecided on that issue.
- A raw `git` spawn in a fixture test bypassing the shared identity-setting helper, passing locally
  (ambient git config) and failing in CI (#1464/#1459). A repo-wide grep found this wasn't a
  recurring backlog (the one instance is already fixed, and a similar file already sets identity
  explicitly), so it didn't clear the bar for either a check or the prose ration this run.
- An unguarded `python3 -c "... s.replace(...) ..."` heredoc edit that printed a success message
  while silently no-op'ing because the target text didn't match (#1452).
- An `AskUserQuestion` showing not-yet-built syntax as a literal example, misread as shipped once
  the question went unanswered across a session boundary (#1473).
- Importing a prior incident's mitigation reasoning into a new case without re-checking the
  triggering condition actually applies there (#1492).

These will recur if they're real; per the extraction method, writing all of them now would spend the
ration past what a single run should.

## Provenance comments posted

- #1444 — cwd-reset rule
- #1461, #1491 — primary-source-before-verdict rule

{"number":1544,"title":"Report an unplaceable declared-check key instead of throwing on it","body":"A key the spec vocabulary cannot place is either a typo or a key a newer engine knows, and the load cannot tell them apart. Refusing it wedged the second case: the declaration lane and the engine lane converge on separate cycles, and the converge that would deliver the vocabulary is itself gated on the load succeeding.

The load now **drops** such a key — with its whole subtree, so a future assertion's nested pattern key is never compiled either — and the new `declared-check-spec-keys` world rule reports it. `advisory` by default, because in a member either reading is possible; this repo overrides it to `blocking` in `.claudinite-settings.json`, where engine and declarations ship from one commit so an unplaceable key can only be a typo. A key the engine *does* place keeps its loud load failure on a broken value (an uncompilable regex, a malformed `since`) — that is not skew, it is broken.

Coded rather than declared: the assertion is "every key, at every level, is in its own container's allowlist" — recursive descent against a per-container vocabulary the declaration language cannot express, and which would have to restate `SPEC_KEYS` as data. It reads the engine's own table instead, and sits beside `declared-check-messages`, which parses the same files for the same reason.

The wedge's three pieces, from the issue: the throw is gone (1), so no load fault is recorded and no rule in the file is dropped (2), so the self-test's `pack-manifests` probe stays green and the converge lands (3). Blast radius for a *broken value* is unchanged — that class still fails loud, deliberately.

In place of the rehearsal fixture the issue asks for, three tests pin the behaviour: the compiled rule keeps running its placed assertions while an unplaceable neighbour is dropped, a member-shaped `.claudinite/local/packs/…/declared-checks.json` carrying a key this engine does not know loads **both** its rules and runs them, and the world rule names the key and its container. Seen failing against a restored throw before being made green.

Closes #1400

{"number":1558,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Refs #1551

The unattended daily `growth-extract` run over this window. Two lessons survive the bar — both from the activity half's merged-PR review discussion — and land as prose in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`:

- **A pack module consuming a brand-new engine helper export** — import the engine module as a namespace and guard the call with a `typeof` capability check, never a named import. #1544 introduced a named import of a fresh engine export; #1549's own body explains why it faulted every member's converge: the pack and engine lanes deliver on separate cadences, so a named import of an export the member's engine hasn't reached yet is a link-time `SyntaxError`. Landed under "The engine, the mount and what reaches members".

- **A regression test that pins a policy or convention decision** — assert the behavior/invariant the decision requires, never a literal sentence quoted from a doc. #1540 (closing #1539) found a test asserting the literal retired sentence "never move a file into `.github/workflows`" — it stayed green through #1511 specifically because it required the contradiction to still be present, letting three artifacts disagree without any check catching it. Landed under "Proving a change".

Both stay prose after the prose-to-checks pass: neither constrains a static signature a declared check could observe with confidence — the first can't distinguish a brand-new engine export from a long-established one without false-positiving on the many existing legitimate named imports from `engine/`, and the second would need semantic judgment about what counts as a "policy sentence" a test shouldn't pin.

### What didn't land, and why

Read in full: the 14 substantive commits, the 18 PRs merged in the window (diff + review discussion), the 5 touched PRs, the 24 touched issues, and the conversation-logs branch's newest 24h window plus the oldest 24h still on the branch (~40 capture files total).

- A park-classification fix (`decision` → `failure`) is already enforced by #1516's own tests — already-settled, not a lesson.
- A staged-migration-record deletion bug (#1545/#1546) traces to the same root cause the corpus already states: "write a coverage marker strictly after the durable effect it guards."
- A solution transferred by analogy without re-checking whether its constraint applied (#1494's `toJSON(vars)` session) dedupes to the existing "verify a claimed architectural rationale against current code" rule.
- A single-repo security config (disabling preview deploys for a token-minting endpoint, #1465) is already enforced by its own deploy file.
- A month-old stale-`origin/main` false-positive on `squash-merge-history` (issues #366/#368/#373, oldest window) is old enough it may already be moot, and the fix would live in engine code, outside this run's write surface.
- Two PRs bundling unrelated concerns and split after the owner objected (#1482, #1531, same day) is one instance of the standing "one concern per commit" rule at PR-scope, not a distinct new principle.
- A cache-key-completeness gotcha (#1465) and a CI-repoll-before-local-repro pattern were real but didn't clear the two-rule ration ahead of the pair above.

No conversation-log rule landed, so no provenance comment is owed on any captured session's issue.

{"number":1561,"title":"writing-pack-prose: the pack-prose authoring skill and the per-pack references doc","body":"Closes #1560

Pack-prose authoring guidance was split across `authoring-agent-docs` (phrasing/findability), `extracting-lessons.md` (the ration), and the local pack's own header (the 40-word format) — and rule rationale had no durable home, leaving `rule-revalidation` nothing to reaffirm judgment rules against.

## What this lands

- **`claudinite-growth/skills/writing-pack-prose`** — one skill owning how pack prose is written, for `RULES.md` and `SKILL.md` alike, local and canon packs: the ration (two one-sentence rules per pass, trigger + directive + consequence), the full shape-a-rule-so-it-fires house style (moved from `authoring-agent-docs`, carried at source strength), the **references convention**, and the **migration procedure** for existing packs (source-first recovery of missing reasons from the adding commit/PR/issue; never invent an entry; unmarked rules stay valid forever, so no fleet sweep is needed).
- **The references convention** — one `references.md` per pack servicing all its prose files and its checks. A rule ends with a bare `(3)` marker (no file name, no link — the doc is for maintenance/review, never daily agentic work); entries are `- **(3)** <reason>` written so a future review can reaffirm the rule (workarounds carry the issue-with-evidence, guidelines cite the original documentation, owner decisions carry the request's language). Numbers are stable identifiers — gaps allowed, never renumbered. Checks join by **reverse pointing** (`- **(check:<id>)**`): the declared-check spec vocabulary is closed and an unknown key is flagged by older fleet engines (`declared-check-spec-keys`), so a new declaration key would buy nothing until every member's engine caught up.
- **`references-integrity`** (worldRule, blocking, `since` 2026-09-01) — every marker resolves to an entry in the pack's own `references.md`, and every `check:` entry names a check the pack still carries. Two-root path form; relevance-first (a pack with no markers produces nothing). Red-first fixtures: the test was watched failing before the module existed; the real tree is clean and only the intended markers match end-of-line `(n)`.
- **`rule-revalidation`** consumes the mechanism: referenced rules and covered checks are reaffirmed against their recorded reasons (workarounds re-probed read-only, guidelines re-checked against their cited docs, owner decisions doc-verified), with retirement proposed in the PR, never decided by the run.
- **First caller** — the canon's own local pack migrates three rules (their inline issue ids move into entries 1–3) and covers its `home-seeded-packs-declared` check, per the migration procedure (the check entry was corrected against the declaration's actual `failureMessage` after a first draft proved invented).
- **`authoring-agent-docs`** narrows to instruction files outside a pack, with a pointer to the new skill; `extracting-lessons.md` slims to bar + routing; the three "evidence never lives here" statements are rewritten to the new decision.
- **Rehearsal fixture** `references` — a member on the convention (markers, multi-citation, a `check:` entry, unmarked legacy rules beside them) converges green, per `consumer-safe-change`'s additive-change remedy: the fixture, not a migration record, because unmarked members are untouched by construction.

## Verification

- `node --test` full suite: 2921 pass, 1 pre-existing shallow-clone guard failure that passes after `--unshallow` (unrelated to this change).
- Rehearsal suite with the new fixture: 66 pass.
- `check_the_work` / `check_the_world`: 0 blocking; the 87 advisories predate this change and none touch its files.

{"number":1645,"title":"Legacy behaves like deprecated: the guideline, the annotation, and the advisories","body":"Closes #1637

A legacy tolerance was the one thing this corpus could add with no removal written and nothing
telling its holders to move. The audit found ~28 declaration sites across `engine/` and `packs/`;
none warned anybody, and `engine/version.mjs` carried a stated end date that had passed six days
earlier with nothing arranged to notice.

## The guideline (`packs/basics`, portable)

`RULES.md` gains one rule — a tolerance is scaffolding: it ships with an advisory firing where the
old shape is still in use, and with its removal already a link in the migration's chain, gated on a
condition that reads back true rather than on a date. The *Planning a migration* bullet names that
removal among the code written before approval, and `writing-migration-plans` gains the section
behind it: the three things that ship with a tolerance, why a date gate fails in both directions,
making an unreadable gate the chain's **first link** rather than a caveat in the removal's brief,
and the asymmetry that decides between a narrow policy and `nothing`.

## The advisories — the half that reaches the holders

| Rule | Reads | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy-shape-in-use` (lifecycle) | the repo's own declaration and stamp | retired file name, `claudinite`/`maintenance` blocks, top-level `packConfig`, `taskScheduler.endpoints`, the `local_packs/` prefix, a renamed pack id, an integer version, the `updates` alias |
| `legacy-task-fields` (tasks) | `tasks/<name>/task.mjs` **source** | `agent_preprocessing*`, `prework*`, `after`, and the one-word outcome ceilings |
| `legacy-check-spellings` (growth) | `declared-checks.json` | the pre-merge `eachValueInParsedArray` spelling |
| `cer/release-workflows` (chrome-extension) | the orchestrator | its tolerated `@main` shape, which used to return silently |

All advisory, permanently: the old shape works, so none of these may stop a member's build. Each
names the edit that moves the repo forward. The task rule reads *source* because the contract's
door renames the fields away before anything downstream can see them — which is exactly what made
that tolerance invisible. Engine constants are namespace-imported and `typeof`-guarded: the two
lanes converge on separate cycles, so a pack sits beside an engine that predates a symbol, and
there the advisory simply drops rather than faulting the pack.

## The annotation — the half that schedules the removal

Every legacy declaration now carries `// @legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule|none> retire:#<issue>`
directly above it, so `grep -rn '@legacy-tolerance' engine packs` **is** the register.
`legacy-tolerance-scheduled` (local pack, blocking after its grace) holds both halves: a tolerance
with nothing above it, and an annotation the register cannot parse. It anchors at column 0, which
is what tells a tolerance point from a `const legacy =` inside a function, and its test runs it
against the real tree rather than only a fixture.

`advisory:none` claims no member file can hold the old shape; the local pack's rule obliges the
retire issue to say what does read the holder instead.

## The removals

#1638 tracks them as four links, each an ad-hoc queue item behind #1639 (the one human step: the
fleet clearance report has to exist in Shepherd before anything here can read a gate) with a
`Not-before:` giving the fleet a month of converges. #1640 and #1641 are `Automerge: nothing` —
a member holding a retired spelling gets *no* pack, loses the `update` task that would deliver its
repair, and the only way back is a hand-run against that repo. #1642 carries a narrow
predicted-folder policy; #1643 stays `nothing` because it spans four packs by construction.

`engine/version.mjs`' tolerance is re-gated here on the fleet's own state rather than the date it
missed.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3127 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world` 0 blocking,
`ci-work-scope` clean. Each new check was seen failing before it was believed: the annotation check
against a stripped annotation in `settings-file-names.mjs`, and `legacy-shape-in-use`'s test with
two of its branches disabled (3 of 11 tests failed).

{"number":1697,"title":"Schedule-board follow-ups: the sim carries the board's state, and two rules","body":"The review of what made #1677's one-sentence request into a 225-line PR found one real coverage gap, one test that should not exist, and two rules worth writing.

**The simulator now carries the board's issue state.** It modelled `{exists, corrupt, rows}`, so "a board found open owes a write even where no row moved" — the half of #1677 that runs on every member's next scheduler run — was invisible to the mechanism's own executable spec. `S61` covers the case a row-driven write cannot reach: a settled repo between anchors, where nothing else brings a write. Seen red first by removing the end-of-run close.

**Dropped the test asserting the rendered body still matches `/closed/i`** — a check that particular text still reads a particular way.

**`writing-tasks` stops naming the board's issue and state.** A task author needs that a decline files no item, not where the record lives; the parenthetical cost `claudinite-growth` a version and a `VERSIONS.md` row every time the queue's bookkeeping changed. It goes in with the rule that forbids it.

**Two rules.** A machine-maintained issue is filed closed and labelled and states both on every write; a pack's prose points at another pack's artifact rather than describing it. Both carry a `references.md` entry with a reaffirm condition.

Rule A went to `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` rather than `claudinite-tasks`: that pack has no `RULES.md`, and opening one would charge every member repo forever for a rule that only fires when authoring the queue's own machinery. Promotion is the growth lane's call if a second repo wants it.

Not here, and described at the foot of the issue if you want them filed: retiring `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` into module headers plus a references doc (56 pointers and a test that parses its headings), and letting PR-time `check_the_world` judge new findings against the merge base so a finding already red on `main` stops blocking every unrelated branch.

Closes #1696

{"number":1711,"title":"Declared checks at every moment: schema rung, work and action scopes, skill triggers, and the creation path","body":"Closes #1699
Closes #1700
Closes #1701
Closes #1702
Refs #1672

Phases 2–5 of the four-moment design (`docs/declarative-checks/DESIGN.md`, landed with Phase 1 in #1676), plus the owner's schema ruling, one commit each.

## The schema rung

Anything a schema can enforce is better handled there. The promotion ladder gains the rung above checks: a document's shape — a required field, a closed value set, a type, a closed key set — lives in the JSON Schema the document points at with `$schema`, and a declared assertion or a coded twin restating it is a schema check in disguise. The engine now enforces it: `engine/checks/helpers/json-schema.mjs` validates the draft-2020 subset the corpus's schemas use, and the basics `schema-conformance` rule judges every JSON document whose `$schema` is a repo-relative path (every task.json in the tree validates; a rehearsal fixture carries a member's own schema-pointed document across). The phrasing is in `extracting-lessons.md`, the `prose-to-checks` skill, basics' ladder line, the checks README, the design and the inventory.

## Phase 2 — work scope (#1699)

`forbidAddedLinesMatching`, `forbidRemovedLinesMatching` (with `unlessMatchRemainsInFile` so a reworded line is not a loss), `requireCoChange`, `flagUntrackedFilesMatching`, and the rule-level `whenReplyClassIncludes` gate on the session's comment classes. Three rules land on them: `check-ships-with-test` (growth, blocking with grace), `untracked-test-file` (basics, advisory — it fired on this branch's own fixtures before they were staged), `rules-append-only` (home, advisory).

## Phase 3 — action scope (#1700)

`scope: "action"` + `guardToolCalls`: a tool, the input field it reads, and the condition. The PreToolUse hook judges the call about to run — blocking denies with the finding's text, advisory injects it as context — and `check_the_work` judges every recorded call at Stop, the backstop and the metric. The hook now watches every tool. Seven guards in basics, seven in the home pack. The shell guards anchor to a command position: the hook's first live firing, in the session that wrote it, was on the phrase inside a commit message. A call the hook denied is recorded advisory at Stop — the firing counted, no block left for the session to clear.

## Phase 4 — trigger scope (#1701)

Skill metadata `force-load-on-tool-calls` (`Bash.command /…/`, a name, or a regex over names), `force-load-on-prompts-matching`, `force-load-on-tool-results-matching`. The PreToolUse guard holds a named call until the skill is loaded; new UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse hooks inject the load instruction; `skill-loaded-before-editing` catches at Stop what a hook never saw; every member registers the two hooks through the converge. A skill counts as loaded by a `Skill` call, a `Read` of its SKILL.md, or a slash command the owner typed (the harness's `<command-name>` block — the same grammar the usage fold reads, pinned by a drift guard). Three operation skills carry rules that had a trigger all along — `committing`, `fetching-from-the-web` (basics), `running-the-suite` (home) — and their bullets leave `RULES.md` by the deletion test (the `rules-append-only` advisories on this branch are those deliberate removals). `writing-handover-issues`, `do-later`, `writing-migration-plans` and `merge-to-main` gain the triggers their descriptions named.

## Phase 5 — the creation path (#1702)

The ladder names the declared rung's three moments and the skill rung's triggers; `prose-to-checks` triages a candidate by where its signature lives (the inventory's classes) before the check-the-world question; the home pack names `docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md` as the sweep's worklist here.

## The hooks are guests (added after review)

The harness reads exit 2 as the one block; any other exit code, a timeout, or stdout that is not JSON is an error printed beside every call it happens on, and `permissionDecision: "allow"` skips the permission prompt. So:

- **One runner.** The three per-call entries are three-line calls into `engine/hooks/hook-runner.mjs`; the judges (`*-judge.mjs`) return verdicts and never touch the process. The runner alone exits — 0, or 2 for a block on an event that can block — and turns a bad payload, an engine that fails to load, a registry that throws or whose import never settles (a 5 s deadline), or a closed stdout into exit 0 and a hook-log line. `engine-tests/hooks/hook-runner.test.mjs` drives every one of those through the real entries; the home pack's `hook-judges-never-exit` check holds the shape.
- **No auto-approval.** The advisory context carries `additionalContext` only; verified live that the harness delivers it without a `permissionDecision`.
- **Cost.** Measured with `dev/tools/hook-latency.mjs` (committed). Before: ~185 ms (PreToolUse) + ~172 ms (PostToolUse) on every call, ~250 ms each with a 5 MB transcript, because each call reloaded the registry and parsed the whole transcript. After: ~88 ms + ~80 ms regardless of transcript size — the active packs' triggers and action rules are cached under the OS temp dir behind a stat fingerprint (settings, pack dirs, manifests, declarations, skills, the deriving engine modules; `engine-tests/hooks/hook-context.test.mjs` proves each edit misses), and the transcript is parsed only once a trigger names the call. The floor is node's start plus the engine imports.
- **The review in a week.** The retrospective brief in the design gained **Hook cost** and **Hook health** rows with the recorded numbers and the durable signal (`hook_non_blocking_error` attachments in the captured transcripts); #1703 is pointed at them.

## Observed in production, in the authoring session

The canon's own hooks run this tree, so each mechanism fired for real while it was being written: a blocking guard denied a Bash call, an advisory guard's context reached the model, the PostToolUse trigger injected a skill's load instruction on a result, and the tool-call trigger held a `node --test` (and later a `git commit`) until the skill was loaded. Those are the plan's verification links V1–V3, read live rather than filed. The runner's fail-open path also ran live: in the minutes between the entries and the judges existing, the hook log shows `done exit=0 hook-failed Cannot find module` and no error reached the call.

## Verified

Rebased onto `main` after #1726: the branch carries no pack version bump or `VERSIONS.md` row (versions are cut on `main`). Full suite green (3357 tests); `check_the_world` at 0 blocking; `check_the_work` at 0 blocking apart from the advisories above; the rehearsal fixtures green in both modes.

{"number":1773,"title":"Date the three action checks added today so they do not convict the past","body":"`git-pull-on-shallow-clone`, `github-api-via-shell` and `merge-main-into-branch` landed in b1363395 (#1711) at 06:49 UTC today, all `blocking`, none carrying `since`.

An action check is re-judged **over the whole session transcript** at Stop, so a blocking one with no creation date convicts calls made before the check existed in the session's tree. That happened within the hour: a `curl … api.github.com` at ~06:45 ran with nothing to stop it — the guard was genuinely not in that checkout — and became a blocking Stop finding at 06:56 once `main` was synced.

And an action finding has **no clearing move**: a file finding is cleared by editing the file, `skill-loaded-before-editing` by loading the skill, but a past tool call cannot be un-made, so it blocks every Stop for the rest of that session.

`applyGrace` is the corpus's own answer — a rule declaring `since` is advisory for `GRACE_DAYS`, on the stated reasoning that *"absence must mean mature, never newborn"*. The pack already follows this for its other recent blocking rules (`legacy-tolerance-scheduled` 2026-09-03, `hook-judges-never-exit` 2026-09-05); today's three simply missed it.

**`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`** — `"since": "2026-09-06"` on those three. They still fire and still say the same thing; they start blocking on the 20th, by which time no session's transcript predates them. `home-seeded-packs-declared` is untouched — it dates from 2026-09-01 and is genuinely mature.

Patched as anchored text, not a re-serialize, so key order and formatting are unchanged (3 insertions, 0 deletions). 59 local-pack tests pass.

Left for its own decision, in the issue: whether a blocking *action* check should ever judge calls from before its `since` at all. Grace expires; the retroactive-transcript problem returns the next time one lands mid-session.

Closes #1772

{"number":1779,"title":"Rules to checks with the four-moment mechanisms: 27 bullets retired across basics, the home pack and canon-curation","body":"Closes #1760
Refs #1672

The conversion pass the owner asked for once #1711 landed, bounded to the three packs every session in this repo loads. Method: the `prose-to-checks` skill's triage and deletion test over the inventory's A–D rows (`docs/declarative-checks/rule-inventory.md`, whose basics and home rows now each record their conversion or the reason they stay).

## Accounting (the session summary's estimator, words ÷ 0.75)

| Pack | bullets retired | trimmed | tokens removed | tokens added |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| basics | 6 | 0 | 477 | 0 |
| claudinite (home) | 18 | 1 | 802 | 25 |
| claudinite-canon-curation | 3 | 2 | 206 | 32 |
| **all** | **27** | **3** | **1485** | **57** |

Net −1428 rule tokens on every session here, on top of #1711's −434.

## 1. The deletion test on prose a landed check already covered

Twelve bullets stood beside the guards #1711 landed. Ten go whole (Grep context, wake-up prompt, pipe-tail, pkill; AskUserQuestion cost, bare sleep, GitHub through the shell, `commit -a`, merge of `main`, rules append-only, `git pull`); one keeps only the half no guard sees (reading a tool result the harness saved to a file); and "Waiting on GitHub CI" goes once the shell guard also sees a `Monitor` poll and a command after `do`/`then`/`else` (a keyword counts only after a separator, after the widened anchor denied its own author's heredoc). The retired rules' reference entries key on their checks now.

## 2. New conversions, each with a violating and a clean fixture

| Prose (pack) | Became | Scope · severity |
|---|---|---|
| Filing an issue that belongs under another (basics) | `sub-issue-without-parent` | action · advisory |
| Searching for a tool with ToolSearch (basics) | the `searching-for-a-tool` skill, loaded on any ToolSearch and on an empty result | trigger |
| Recording a migration's plan… never a MIGRATION.md (home) | `migration-record-in-docs` | world · blocking |
| Wanting to verify or read something across members (home) | `cross-repo-verify-line` | action · advisory |
| Wanting to read a public sibling repo (home) | `add-repo-for-a-public-clone` | action · advisory |
| Sending a screenshot rendered from a scratch harness (home) | `scratch-screenshot-caption` | action · advisory |
| Checking whether an actor may trigger… never `author_association` (home) | `author-association-as-permission` | world · blocking |
| Changing an export in `updates/*` (home) | `updates-export-removed` | work · blocking |
| Picking a compact date-encoded identifier (home) | `year-last-digit-rollover` | world · blocking |
| Mutating a file to see a check fail (home) | `checkout-restores-index` | action · advisory |
| Editing a repo's JSON config (home) | `settings-json-reserialized` | action · advisory |
| Naming a new canon pack — kebab-case half (curation) | `pack-directory-kebab-case` | world · blocking |
| Wanting to state how many checks or rules (curation) | `corpus-count-in-prose` | world · advisory |
| Wanting prose in a check declaration (curation) | already covered by basics' `declared-check-spec-keys`; the coverage is now a tested claim, not a reasoned one | — |
| A canon pack's prose naming another pack — the home-only half (curation) | `home-only-path-in-canon-prose` | world · blocking |
| A pack module consuming a brand-new engine export (curation) | `named-import-of-new-engine-export`, a work-scope two-pass over the change's added engine exports | work · blocking |

Every blocking check carries `since: 2026-09-06`, so it advises for two weeks. The vocabulary gains one key, `forbidTrackedPathsMatching` (the mirror of `requirePaths`), with its engine test.

## 3. Attempted and withdrawn

`history-test-shallow-guard` (a test walking git history must guard a shallow clone) fired on six real tests, every one walking the history of a fixture repo it created itself. Fixture history cannot be told from the real repository's by a static signature, so the check is withdrawn and the bullet stays, with the reason on its inventory row.

## 4. Logged, not converted

Twenty-three rows, each with its reason in the inventory. The recurring reasons: the mark needs a fact no input carries (a diff's implied folders, a queue item's issue number, an open PR this session); a literal ban has legitimate hits today (`missingbulb/` in the canon URL and a migration record, `Number(doc.version)` on an integer format); the rule is judgment wearing a form (describes-vs-instructs, "a literal sentence"); or the one sanctioned exception would need a silent `excludeFiles` a declaration cannot explain.

## 5. The Stop backstop is advisory (a design correction surfaced by this work)

Widening a guard mid-session re-judged a call that had already run, and the Stop hook blocked on a finding no edit could clear. The transcript is append-only, so `actionFindings` now records every guard finding at Stop as advisory — the count and the diagnosis — and the hook, where a block still prevents the call, is the one place the declared severity blocks. A denied call's finding says so. The design and the checks README carry the rule.

## Standing hit

`migration-record-in-docs` finds `docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md`, the one tracked violation; #1775 retires it into #390 and waits on this PR.

## Verified

Full suite green (3249 tests). `check_the_world` 0 blocking: the new checks fire only on that standing hit. `check_the_work` 0 blocking; its advisories are the `rules-append-only` records of these deliberate removals and the session's own guard firings.

{"number":1793,"title":"Say the hold's unreadable variable once, and keep verifications inside this repo","body":"Two owner reports, one branch.

## 1. The hold's live read repeated its refusal at every boundary

```
! could not read CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL live (403) — using the value this run started with. …
```

The between-items read (`queue/suspend.mjs`, DESIGN §15.30) asks
`GET /repos/{repo}/actions/variables/…` at each pick. That endpoint is scoped to a token's
variables access, which the workflow `permissions:` block has no key for — DESIGN §15.24 already
said so — so on the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` the read is refused at every boundary of every drain,
permanently. The line reported the same standing fact once per item, and spent an API call each
time to re-learn it.

`readSuspendedNow` becomes `liveSuspendReader`, a per-run reader: an access refusal (401/403) is a
fact about this run's token, so it is said once and never asked again; anything else (a 5xx) keeps
asking, because a blip says nothing about the token, but is still printed once. The hold's reach is
unchanged — a drain that cannot read it live degrades exactly as it did before the drain batched.
The DESIGN and SCENARIOS lines that described the old per-boundary behaviour are corrected.

Closes #1791

## 2. A verification filed here cannot read another member's repository

#1790 verified janitor rule I against `missingbulb/TLDR#275` with a coded probe on
`api.github.com`. `verify-production`'s `fetchOnce` sends no credential, so that read answers
anonymously — rate-limited from an Actions runner, and 404 for anything not public — and an agentic
session's scope names this repository alone. The item could never pass; it would re-arm every six
hours forever. The wall is target-repo permissions, not egress, which is why it is invisible from a
session that can reach the URL with its own credentials.

- The `cross-repo-verify-line` guard already watched the agentic `Verify:` line; it now watches the
  coded form's `Live-probe:`/`Verify-probe:` lines for `api.github.com` too — the structurally
  identical sibling. A member's public raw or Pages URL stays fine, and is pinned as a non-firing
  case.
- The local pack states the two ways out: reproduce the premise on an object this repo owns, or
  file the verification on the target repo. It is a local rule rather than a canon one because
  other members' routines may hold wider scope.
- #1790 itself is rewritten against this repo's own three abandoned failure parks (#1146, #1271,
  #1362), which cross rule I's ten-day bound on 2026-09-11.

Closes #1792

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`: 3300 pass, 1 fail — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which
refuses a shallow clone and fails the same way on an untouched tree. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking.

{"number":1812,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth-extract run over the window in #1810 (commits 1c5205f..5050608, PRs #1612-#1800, plus the fresh-24h and oldest-24h conversation-log windows on `origin/conversation-logs`).

## What landed — two rules, ration-capped

**Activity half.** PR #1733's own body records a design mistake in its *first* draft, not its landed shape: the `preconditions` field's original shape was retired on review as cryptic — `["none"]` and no key at all were a keystroke apart and meant opposite things, and that ambiguity is how one call site answered a scheduling question wrong. That's a generalizable declaration-design lesson distinct from the substance of the landed rewrite (which is already captured by the commit itself), so it gets its own rule: RULES-72.

**Conversation half.** Across the fresh-24h window (33 captures) and the oldest-24h hindsight window (6 captures, all already covered by existing rules), one new pattern cleared the bar: issue-1672's capture shows a worktree-isolated agent hitting the Bash worktree-isolation guard's "too complex to verify" refusal nine times over ~29 minutes (22:31–23:01 UTC), retrying a different clever wrapper each time — a `for` loop, two heredocs, three shapes of computed substitution (`$(git ls-files ...)`, `$(cat ...)`, `xargs -a`) — around the same git call, instead of dropping to the plain literal form the guard accepts. Lands as RULES-73.

A third candidate (issue-1727: 70 `skill-not-loaded` denials over ~5 minutes from editing a multi-pack test sweep file-by-file instead of surveying the sweep's full file list and preloading every skill it would force) was real but weaker in magnitude than the two above, and the ration is two rules per run — dropped per the rule; it will recur if it's real.

## Prose-to-checks upgrade pass

Ran over this run's own two additions only. Neither has a static signature a declared check could carry: RULES-72 is a design-time judgment call (no post-hoc scan can tell whether a given pair of field values is "ambiguous enough"), and RULES-73's trigger depends on session-isolation context (whether the agent is worktree-isolated) that the check DSL has no way to condition on — firing the same pattern-match unconditionally would be noise in the vast majority of non-isolated sessions where a loop or heredoc around `git` is completely normal. Nothing converted.

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3354/3354 green.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking; the run's own two new lines are both under the 100-byte `rules-line-length` advisory threshold.

{"number":1827,"title":"Land two lessons from #1317's revalidation","body":"Closes #1826

Two rules into `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`, with their reference entries. Two is the ration, so the weaker candidates are dropped rather than squeezed in.

## RULES-74 — read the world, not the link's issue

> **Judging whether a migration chain's link is still outstanding** — read the world its exit condition names, never the link's own issue: the fleet converged L1–L3 unattended and the code landed the destructive L4 while all six issues still read `blocked` thirteen days later.

This is the friction that prompted the session. #1317 read as stalled since 2026-08-25 with four members un-repointed. In fact all 13 members had converged, every workflow named the pack paths, and the L4 deletion had landed on 2026-08-24 — without its own PR, since #1329 closed unmerged. Two triage passes reaffirmed the stalled reading from the issues alone. One shallow clone per member settled it.

## RULES-75 — a removed-line check cannot see a removed file

> **Writing a check that fires on a removed line** (`forbidRemovedLinesMatching`) — it cannot see a deleted file: `removedLines` returns nothing for a path git no longer tracks, so removing one export fires and deleting the whole module is silent.

Measured both ways against #1819's branch:

| Change | `updates-export-removed` |
|---|---|
| one `export *` line removed, file survives | fires |
| all six modules of `updates/` deleted | silent |

Cause is `repo-context.mjs:639` — `if (!mergeBase || !tracked.includes(file)) return []`, and a deleted file is not tracked.

The engine-side fix would change every `forbidRemovedLinesMatching` rule in the corpus at once (`rules-append-only` included), so it is filed as **#1823** rather than folded in here.

## Verification

Suite 3362 pass / 0 fail; `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking. No pack version or `VERSIONS.md` row touched — a local pack is neither versioned nor distributed, and the commit is the record.

{"number":1782,"title":"Rule revalidation: re-probe five harness claims at their live addresses","body":"Refs #1767

Rebased onto current `main` and rewritten. This now also carries the still-valid corrections from #1441 and #1283, which are closed as folded in.

## Why it was rewritten

Three revalidation PRs — this one, #1441 and #1283 — each rewrote **the same** `ToolSearch` bullet in `packs/basics/RULES.md`, with three different answers. That bullet is no longer in `main`: it became the `searching-for-a-tool` skill, and the `Grep` bullet beside it became the `grep-context-without-content` guard. All three were correcting text `main` had already moved, which is why all three conflicted and why none of them could land.

Every claim below was re-probed live in this session, and each correction lands where the prose lives **today**.

## Corrected

| Claim as it stood | Probe | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| `searching-for-a-tool`: "the bare short name returns 'no matching tools'" | `select:get_teams` → "No matching deferred tools found"; `get_teams` → the tool's full schema, with `mcp__github__get_teams` in the listing throughout | The two forms differ: `select:` matches fully-qualified names **only**, a bare short name is a keyword query and resolves. The old text named the working form as the failing one. |
| `basics` `Calling Edit`: "the file must have been read *with the read tool*" | A scratchpad file **outside** the working directory, written by a Bash `printf` and never opened with Read, edited successfully — result: "file state is current in your context" | The requirement is the content being current in the session; a session write satisfies it as a read does. |
| `github-api-via-shell` + 3 prose sites: "this sandbox proxy-blocks `api.github.com`" | `/rate_limit` → **200**. `/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite`, its `/pulls/1782`, `/commits/main/check-runs` and public `/repos/nodejs/node` → **403** `{"message": "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"}`. Separately, `command -v gh` → absent | Not egress — authorization, and only for repo-scoped paths. The guard's advice is unchanged and its 26-minute evidence stands; the stated cause was wrong. Recorded besides: reaching the host proves nothing, so a reachability probe reassures while the real call still fails. The guard's other arm (`gh `) holds for a different reason, so the message now names both. |
| `running-the-suite`: "`node --test <dir>` does not recurse" (grouped with the bash glob as equally silent) | node v22.22.2: `node --test <dir>` exits 1 with `Error: Cannot find module <dir>` | It fails outright. The bash glob is the one that leaves you believing a green run over 37 of 65 files, and the rule now says so. |

## Holds — no edit needed

- **Grep context flags.** #1782's original correction was right that a guard now blocks the call, but `main` had already deleted the bullet in favour of `grep-context-without-content`. Nothing to change.
- The four "Holds" probed by this PR's earlier run (`ScheduleWakeup` `prompt`, `sub_issue_id`, `Closes #n` and the Development panel, the Bash `cd` reset) are unchanged and still hold.

## What did not survive from the folded PRs

#1441's Edit claim — that a prior read is no longer required at all because the harness tracks any inspection — is not what the probe shows, and is contradicted by the Edit tool's own current description. The rule keeps its "read it first when neither has happened" clause.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **3372 pass, 0 fail**. (`engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` caught the `Calling Edit` word-count row at 54 vs 55; fixed, re-run green.)
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**, exit 0; no finding names any file this PR touches.
- Re-run on a scratch merge with current `main`, since the world sweep is judged post-merge and this PR changes a check's message: **3375 pass, 0 fail, 0 blocking**.
- The reworded guard's own fixture test (`action-guards.test.mjs`) — 5 pass.
- Every correction carries a `references.md` entry with its probe and the condition that would retire it.

{"number":1836,"title":"The janitor is a fallback, and a rejected terminal closes its issue","body":"Closes #1835

Two halves of one owner ruling.

## The charter

The janitor is a **fallback** — cleanup. Every rule it runs repairs something that already went wrong; no stage of a task's healthy flow passes through it; and an item somebody **closed**, park label and all, is finished rather than a state to repair. Written where the next author reads it: `janitor-rules.mjs`'s header, the task's `README.md`, DESIGN §11's opening, and one rule in this repo's local pack.

## A terminal closes the issue it stands on

> A task that has its PR closed and not merged, and the issue remained open — should be closed by the janitor to say the task was rejected.

Janitor rule G's unmerged half now closes the item `not_planned`, marked or filed, and so does the executor's own decline. That retires #1489's second half (§16.5's "a rejected terminal stands on the open issue, because the run's verdict is not the issue's validity") — a decision rule H (#1526) was already overriding a day later with a second comment, so it only survived in the corpus. Recorded as DESIGN decision §15.34; re-asking is unchanged — clear the status.

`AUTOMERGE: nothing` — it changes a standing design decision.

## Folders touched

| folder | what changed |
|---|---|
| `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` | `executor.mjs`'s `close()` no longer exempts a marked issue from a non-`done` terminal; `janitor-rules.mjs` gains the charter and rule G's both-outcomes-close reading; `implement-request/preconditions.mjs`'s refusal comment follows |
| `packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/` | rule G's shell closes on either resolution; the README opens with what this task is |
| `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/tasks-dispatch/` | DESIGN §11's charter, §16.1/§16.5 restated, decision §15.34 added; SCENARIOS S45 follows |
| `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/` | two rules — the janitor as fallback lane, and a terminal closing its issue — with their `references.md` entries |

## Verification

Both changed assertions were seen to fail first. `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` green (3385 pass), `check_the_work --changed` and `check_the_world` report no blocking finding.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

The repo ledger's queue-closes figure counts an issue closed wearing only a park as `none` — "closed without converging at all", flagged bad. Under this ruling that is a legitimate end, so the bucket miscounts a person's own close. Filed separately rather than reshaping a stored series here.

{"number":1850,"title":"Gate a removed engine or pack export — the surface neither rehearsal can see","body":"Closes #1848

#1750 (`db9981f`) removed nine exports from `engine/converge-wiring.mjs`. Three of them — `BADGE_ROW_START`, `BADGE_ROW_END`, `README` — are imported by Shepherd's own world rule, so last night's converge delivered an engine its local pack could not load: `check_the_world` reported it blocking under `config`, the converged tree failed its self-test, and missingbulb/Shepherd#477 parked `needs-human`.

## Why nothing caught it

Member local-pack code importing the mount is a real, corpus-encouraged contract that nothing treated as one.

- **The live canary** — `ClaudiniteCanary`'s local pack imports nothing out of `.claudinite/shared/`; `realism-artifacts.mjs:12` states it as a design property. A rehearsal converges it green whatever the export surface does.

{"number":1883,"title":"Correct the maintenance-PR rule: it is a repo setting, and CI reads as unstarted","body":"Closes #1882

The rule at `RULES.md:283` ended **"not a missing repo setting"**. It is one — Actions → General → *Approval for running fork pull request workflows from contributors*, set to **Require approval for first-time contributors**, is what parks the run. The clause was aimed at auto-merge being disabled (the other shape `land-pr.mjs:327` names), but as written it sends the reader away from the true cause.

It also named the wrong symptom. `unstable` is the cheap one. What cost time twice this week is the gated run being the **only** check GitHub shows, so the PR reads as *CI never started*:

| | cost |
|---|---|
| missingbulb/Shepherd#477 | ~21h before the run was approved |
| missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1185 | an owner round-trip asking why CI hadn't started |

Both resolve on one read — the runs on the head sha, where the queue's own `workflow_dispatch` run (`land-pr.mjs:602`) sits beside the phantom and is the real CI.

## Why not just loosen the setting

Weighed and declined (owner, 2026-09-07). missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1160 had a green dispatch run beside a gated phantom and **merged one cycle later** — the gate delays, it has not lost a merge. Loosening it is per-repo manual work across the fleet that weakens fork-PR protection on public repos to save a cycle on bot PRs.

## The diff

```
- **Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land** — `unstable` beside a green sweep is a
-   parked `action_required` run, not a missing repo setting.
+ **Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR whose checks look wrong** — CI apparently never started,
+   or `unstable` beside a green sweep — read the runs on its head sha: the queue dispatches its
+   own, so a lone `action_required` beside one is a gated phantom that never executed, and costs a
+   cycle rather than the merge. (80)
```

Plus the `(RULES-80)` entry carrying the evidence and its retirement condition.

**`rules-append-only` reports the rewritten subject line as an advisory.** Deliberate — a correction to a false clause, which is what its `fix` text asks be said here.

## Verification

- Whole suite green (3395 tests); `check_the_world` 0 blocking; `check_the_work` 0 blocking, the one advisory above.

{"number":1951,"title":"Drop pr_name; keep the rule, and simplify the growth policies","body":"Closes #1977
Closes #1978

**This pull request no longer adds `pr_name`.** That feature is dropped — no task declares one, nothing was waiting for it, and reviewing it turned up two hazards that existed only because the field did (#1952, #1953, both closed with it). The branch is reset to `main`. What is left is the two things worth keeping, one commit each.

### A new declared property is judged on its own terms (#1977)

A property added to a declared vocabulary must not have its meaning depend on a sibling property's value — not in a validation, a default, a behaviour, or the prose describing it. An interaction between two properties is the owner's call to permit, never the author's to infer. The task contract's three existing pairs (`automerge`/`expected_outcome`, `agent_instructions`/`agent_model`, `code_work_timeout`/`code_work`) are named in the rule as standing, rather than claiming a cleanliness the tree does not have.

Prose rather than a check: a check here would have to assert that validation code does not read a sibling field, which is the "asserts particular code still reads a particular way" shape this repo rejects.

### The four growth tasks auto-merge one scope (#1978)

`growth-extract`, `growth-dedup`, `prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` each declared a different policy, three of them narrowing the folder scope with a diff-class intersection. Those intersections encoded a guess about the diff's *shape* — extract only adds, the sweep only removes lines, dedup only trims — on top of the folder scope that is the thing worth constraining, and each guess was a second gate a correct run could fail.

All four now declare `["under:.claudinite/local"]`: the repo's own Claudinite tree, any change of any kind, nothing outside it. `.claudinite-settings.json` stays out — these tasks read it and write none of it. The two policy tests that pinned the removed guesses now assert the scope that replaced them.

Full suite green: 3436 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world` reports 0 blocking.

{"number":2015,"title":"Read each window commit's detail once per scheduler run","body":"Every commit-derived signal collector resolved a window commit's file list with its own API read, and the scheduler collects signals once per task, so one run read the same immutable object once per task that windows on commits. On the 2026-09-13 10:35 scheduler run that was 13 tasks over a 40-commit weekly window: ~4 m 40 s of a 4 m 55 s job on sequential `/commits/{sha}` reads. The `commits` collector also ignored the window the collection had already resolved into `ctx.commits`, doubling its own share.

## What changed

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/index.mjs`: the detail read is memoised per reader for the life of the process, keyed on repo and sha. Only a 200 is kept, so a rate limit or a 5xx is the next collector's to retry rather than the run's verdict. A separate reader (a fleet reader over another repo, a test's fake `gh`) never sees a sha another one resolved. The `commits` collector now reads `ctx.commits` like its siblings.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/signals.test.mjs`: three tests, watched failing first — a second collection reads no commit detail again, a failed read is retried rather than pinned, and two readers never share a sha.

{"number":2030,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Window: the thirteen substantive commits of 2026-09-14's run (#2026), the pull requests they landed, and the captures on `conversation-logs` for the last 24 hours plus the first 24 hours still on the branch (2026-07-19/20, the hindsight pass).

## What landed — one check, no prose

`shell-write-to-skill-scoped-path`, an **advisory** action guard in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite`.

**The friction.** `engine/hooks/pretooluse-judge.mjs:45` holds a file edit until its path-scoped skill is loaded — but `FILE_TOOLS` is `Edit`, `Write`, `NotebookEdit` only. #1648 designed it that way and accepted a `check_the_work` backstop for "edits made through Bash, which the hook cannot see". The measurement says that backstop is now the common path, not the exception:

| | |
|---|---|
| attended sessions captured on 2026-09-13 | 13 |
| Bash calls across them | 1755 |
| sessions making **zero** `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` calls | 12 |
| sessions collecting a blocking `skill-loaded-before-editing` finding at Stop | 10 |

Every repo edit in those sessions went through `cat > packs/…/RULES.md`, `python3 - <<'PY'` or `sed -i`, so the skill requirement arrived at Stop — after the work it was there to shape — and each finding cost a load plus a re-read of what had already been written. The unattended queue sessions in the same window used `Edit` heavily (7–22 calls each) and collected none.

**The guard.** A Bash `command` whose text puts a write construct — a `>`/`>>` redirect, an `open(`/`Path(`, or a quoted assignment — directly in front of a path the corpus scopes to a skill (`*.test.*`, `RULES.md`, `SKILL.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `tasks/**`, `engine/checks/**`). Its `fix` is the one-line remedy: write it with `Write`, or `Edit` after a read.

**Tuning is measured, not guessed.** The regex was run against the window's own 1755 captured commands: 93 hits, of which one is a read (`taskPath="packs/basics/tasks/…/task.md"` inside a `node -e` `existsSync`). Two earlier drafts were rejected by that corpus — an unprefixed path alternation fired on `grep --include=RULES.md`, and a bare `VAR=path` branch fired on three `sed -n` reads.

**Advisory rather than blocking**, deliberately: a bulk sweep across many scoped files (the 2026-09-13 `rules-line-length` reflow is the window's own example) is a legitimate shell job this regex cannot tell from a single-file rewrite, and denying it would wedge real work. The rationale and its retirement condition are in `references.md`.

**Red-first.** The guard was weakened (prefix group emptied, `RULES.md`/`SKILL.md`/`CLAUDE.md` dropped) and the fixture went red at `2 !== 4`; restoring it returned 7/7. ## What this does

`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/sim.mjs` was a second implementation of the
dispatch mechanism beside `queue/`: its own scheduler run, its own pick order, its
own claim arbitration, its own anchor arithmetic, its own janitor. This deletes
that model. `sim.mjs` is now the wiring between the fake world H1 (#1347) built
and the real entry points — `schedulerRun`, `runExecutor`, `sweepQueue`,
`continueOrEscalate`, `convergeOps`, the precondition engine and the anchor
arithmetic are imported and run, and every one of the 81 scenarios drives them.

**Exit reads, on this branch:**

- `sim.mjs` contains no `schedulerRun` implementation, no `janitor(`, no
  `pickable(`, no `claim(` and no anchor arithmetic of its own — 1481 lines of
  model became 838 lines of wiring.
- every scenario green (81 titles, all the old ones kept), the claim guard green
  both ways, `check_the_world` 0 blocking, `check_the_work` clean, the whole suite
  green: **3671 tests, 0 failures**.

Rebased onto `main` at `4efc4c8`, which had independently instrumented the two
modules this branch reshapes: `startRunCost`/`runCost` in `src/execute/loop.mjs`,
and the phase timings inside the `main()` body `src/schedule/run.mjs` now extracts.
Resolved by unioning the cost parameters with the `timers` seam, and by making
`phase` an injected seam on `schedulerRun` so the cost record stays in the argless
`main()` wrapper. The count above is the post-rebase run.

## What it found

The link says a disagreement between the model and the code is the finding, and
that the code being wrong makes the fix part of the change. Four disagreements;
three of them were the code.

**1. An executor converges an item it was reclaimed off.**
`src/execute/loop.mjs` re-verified nothing after the work step. The work step is
the one phase that may legally outlive the executing leash, and the beat that
keeps a live holder out of the reclaim is fail-soft by design — a partitioned
runner keeps working while its beats fail to post. Driven for real, S31b does not
livelock as `PRINCIPLES.md` claimed: it double-executes, and at minute 130 the
zombie closes the item `done` while its replacement is forty minutes into the same
work. Re-entrant code-work makes the second RUN safe and says nothing about a
second CONVERGE. Fixed: the stale runner re-verifies its claim and abandons
silently.

**2. A session's park leaves no episode boundary.**
A departing executor strikes its own claim; a session cannot — the claim is the
executor's and a session has no edit for it. So every claim of the parked episode
outlived the park, and the next executor to claim the re-queued item lost the race
to a dead claim, on its first try and on every try after it. That is F18 reached
through the one converge that had no way to say it had let go; S49 walks straight
into it. Fixed: the boundary rides the converge comment, a marker `claimWinner`
already reads whatever wrote it.

**3. Queue membership is gated on a label the requester can remove.**
`isQueueItem` counted an adopted marked issue only while it wore the mark. A
requester who takes their own label off drops the item out of every read of the
queue at once — never picked, never declined, and invisible to the janitor's
rules, which cannot sweep what they cannot list. S48's premise found it. Fixed by
widening to either artifact adoption wrote, which is the same "three signals, any
one sufficient" shape `converge-item`'s own refusal already took, for the same
reason (missingbulb/Shepherd#360).

**4. `S41` — the claim was wrong, not the code.**
`PRINCIPLES.md` said a worker naming its failure kind parks there. #1452
deliberately retired that: a failed run parks `failure` whatever the worker asked
for, because a worker naming `action` put a failed run in a non-blocking lane and
the task re-filed the next morning against a cause nobody had fixed. The verdict
now reaches the person in the park's comment. The claim is corrected; the
scenario asserts both halves.

Three more corrections of the same kind, smaller: S48 (the sanctioned withdrawal
is the mark **and** the status, as adoption's own comment instructs), S65 (there
is no close-time drain — the engine's only dispatch sites are the scheduler's
drain job and the failure continuation, so the chain's tail waits for the next
tick), and S77 (`create-work-item` stamps `Woken:` on every item it makes; what it
*refuses*, and so what nothing stamps, is an unqualified item of a scheduled task).

## The speed claim, restated

The link asked for 5 s over the whole `test/sim/` set. That figure was set against
a model that made no API calls. Driving the real engine costs about 3 ms per
scheduler tick, so `S21` alone — five quiet weeks, 859 ticks — is 2.6 s and the set
is ~13 s. The claim is stated per scenario instead, where it holds and where a
wall-clock wait creeping in actually shows up: **S80** asserts that a simulated
working day costs milliseconds and waits for nothing. Restating the budget is the
one place this PR changes what the link asked for, and it is stated here so it can
be overruled.

## Why this parks for review

The link authorizes `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/docs`.
This diff reaches outside it, deliberately and on the link's own instruction that a
fix to the code is part of the change:

So it is one PR under the policy, and the policy failing is the speed bump that
puts a person back on the trail rather than an error to route around.

## The diff is wider than the ask

Six folders: `src/schedule/`, `src/execute/`, `src/items/`, `src/session/`,
`src/world/`, `test/sim/`, plus `docs/` and one local-pack rule. The abstraction

had one; the scheduler run did not, and giving it one is most of the non-test
diff. The three correctness fixes are each in a different module because the
three failures are: that is what deleting a model buys, and it is not something

## The check — `subagent-branch-named-git` (blocking, `since: 2026-09-16`)

A worktree-isolated child dispatched "on a branch named `perf/git-fixtures`" could not create that branch. From the capture on #2074 (session `f3d8d7fb`, 15:04:05–15:05:24), eight attempts refused:

| attempt | form |
|---|---|
| `git checkout -b perf/git-fixtures origin/main` | plain |
| `git switch -c perf/git-fixtures origin/main` | plain, other verb |
| `inwt.sh git switch -c perf/git-fixtures origin/main` | script wrapper |
| `exec "$(command -v g''it)" "$@"` | splice around the token |
| `git branch -m perf/git-fixtures` | rename after the fact |
| `git branch -m "perf/git-fixtures"` | quoted |
| `echo <sha> > $D/refs/heads/perf/git-fixtures` | direct ref write (permission classifier) |

`git switch -c perf/xtmp origin/main` passed first try — which is the contrast that makes the *name*, not the command shape, the cause. The child then handed back asking the parent to rename the branch for it.

`RULES-73` already covers varying the **wrapper** around a refused call; nothing covered the case where the argument itself carries the token, and there the advice it gives ("drop to the plain, literal form") is the form that had already failed. The dispatch is the only moment the name is still cheap to change, so the guard sits there: an `Agent` call whose input carries `"isolation":"worktree"` and whose prompt mandates a branch whose own name has a `git` segment.

**Fixtures, both directions.** The separator in the character class is what the check turns on — `perf/git-fixtures` fires, `claude/digit-fix` does not. Weakening the `match` drops the two mandating dispatches; dropping the separator flags the `digit` case. Both were watched red before landing.

```
silent #0 Inventory issue-first assumptions   isolation=undefined
FIRES  #1 "branch named `perf/git-fixtures"
silent #2 Stop spawning node in tests         isolation=worktree
silent #3 Queue simulator hot loop            isolation=worktree
silent #4 Analyse two engine optimizations    isolation=worktree
silent #5 Lazy buildContext                   isolation=worktree
silent #6 Cache the queue signal probes       isolation=worktree
silent #7 Split the dispatch resolver         isolation=worktree
```

Six other worktree-isolated dispatches in the same fan-out — `perf/test-spawns`, `perf/sim-loop`, `perf/lazy-ctx`, `perf/signal-probes`, `perf/dispatch-split` — name branches the child could spell, and stay silent.

{"number":2110,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Two rules and one skill line into `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`, from the 2026-09-17 window — its one substantive commit (`c41ed6c`), the pull requests merged and touched in it, and both conversation-log windows (the last 24 hours: four captures; the oldest 24 hours still on the branch: six, 2026-07-19/20).

Advances #2104.

## RULES-93 — a format change that orders itself needs no migration

- **Changing the format of an identifier members compare for order** — choose the new shape so every old value already sorts below every new one (one more digit does it), and the change needs no migration, no legacy tolerance and no convergence window.

**Evidence** — #2100, the window's one substantive commit. `cloudflare-site`'s release minor was a bare `MMDD`, which runs backwards every New Year (`1231` then `0101`), so "later means bigger" stopped being true once a year. The fix counted years from a fixed epoch *in front of* the month and day, which took the minor from at most four digits to at least five: every adopter's next release sorts above its last whatever date it lands on, so the change shipped with no renumbering, no cutover, and no tolerance to retire later.

**Why it earns a rule here** — this repo already knows it cannot census its members to decide when a tolerance may go (RULES-12), so the tolerance stands forever and the window never reads true. A representation that orders itself is the escape from that, and it is chosen at design time or not at all. It is a design judgment with no static signature, so it lands as prose rather than a check.

## RULES-94 — a conformance sweep reports every fault, not the first

- **Writing a conformance test that quantifies over the shelf or the tree** — gather every member's failure and assert once at the end; one that throws inside the loop reports a single fault per run, so a change touching five packs pays five red-green cycles.

**Evidence** — the capture on #2089 (session `2f6cc995`, 20:44:14–20:47:13). A growth-promote run added six rules across five canon packs without their README rule-index rows. `engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs`'s first subtest loops the shelf and `assert.equal`s inside the loop, so each run named exactly one pack: the session re-ran that one file six times over ~3 minutes, learning its five faults one at a time, to collect what one iteration would have reported together.

**Not converted** — the signature (an `assert` reached inside a loop over a discovered set) is indistinguishable from an ordinary loop over a fixture list, where failing on the first case is correct. Detection cannot be made confident, so per the upgrade pass's own rule the candidate stays prose.

## `running-the-suite-5` — the test that guards a pack's prose is not under `packs/`

- **Editing a `RULES.md` or `README.md` under `packs/`** — the file that holds a pack's rule index in step with its prose sits outside the pack, and neither conformance sweep runs it, so add `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches.

**Evidence** — the same run. Before pushing it cleared `check_the_world`, `check_the_work`, the edited pack's own suite and `engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs` — none of which reads a README's rule index — and heard about the missing rows from CI four minutes later. Nothing in the path of `packs/<pack>/RULES.md` points at `engine-tests/`, so this is exactly the covering test an "run what the edit touches" heuristic cannot find; it lands at the skill rung, under `running-the-suite`'s existing `node --test` trigger, rather than as prose every session pays for.

## The co-change check I did not ship

The obvious conversion for the incident above is a `scope: "work"` `requireCoChange`: an added `- **` line in `packs/*/RULES.md` requires some changed `packs/*/README.md`. Measured against the 60 commits this checkout carries, four touched a pack's `RULES.md` bullets and one of those four — `e739e6e` — **rewords** a rule's lead-in rather than adding one, needing no README change at all and leaving the tree green. `requireCoChange` cannot see a net count, so the check would have been wrong on 1 in 4 real cases. Not confident, so not shipped.

## Verification

- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — silent; `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, and no advisory names a file this change touches.
- Whole suite, `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`: `# pass 3730`, `# fail 0`.
- `merge-policy-run.mjs --base origin/main --policy 'under:.claudinite/local'` → `AUTOMERGE: yes — every changed file is covered`.

No local-pack changelog file: the commit and this PR are the record.

{"number":2160,"title":"Claudinite growth: dedup local packs","body":"Weekly dedup of `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/` against the canon this repo mounts. Three items pruned, each with the canon line that covers it. Refs #2148.

## 1. Removed — `Writing a docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md`

Was:

> the end state and its rationale only, with alternatives and their drawbacks. Never requests, prior-state narrative, or owner opinions.

Covered by `packs/basics/skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md`:

> **The design doc** (`docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md`, where the project keeps one) describes the **end state and its rationale** — what the mechanism is once the work is done, and why that shape over the alternatives, with each alternative's drawbacks stated. It never carries the previous state as narrative, the requests or conversation that led here, owner attributions or opinions, progress, or a phase list.

The canon says everything the local rule said and more (progress, a phase list, the reader test), in the same path spelling, so there was no narrower case left in the local copy. The skill declares `force-load-on-file-edits-paths: ['docs/**/DESIGN.md']`, so it loads at exactly the moment the rule fired. The two neighbouring local rules — what to do with a design doc whose system is now built, and sweeping its `§`-numbered pointers — say things the canon does not, and stay.

## 2. Removed — `Converging a work item from a session`

Was:

> `converge-item.mjs` prints the calls; making them verbatim with your own GitHub tools is the whole path, on every session, with or without a REST route. Hand-fabricating the transition is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status, or labelled `done` and left open. (2)

Covered by `packs/claudinite-tasks/public/instructions.md`, the file every session executing a work item reads:

> **Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand.** … **The command decides the transition; you perform it.** It does not touch GitHub, and it is not trying to: your GitHub access is yours, and a subprocess you spawn cannot reach it. … Then **make the calls it printed, in the order given, changing nothing** … If the command refuses, read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status.

Same directive, same failure-mode sentence, and the canon also carries the "with or without a REST route" half as its reason. Its `(2)` rationale entry goes with it in `references.md`; per the references convention the number is retired rather than reused.

## 3. Stripped — `Ending a session on unfinished work`

Was:

> write the state into the PR, or into the tracking issue when the work has one; the owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`. Never compose a hand-off prompt.

The first half is `packs/basics/RULES.md`:

> **Ending a session with the change unfinished** — write the state where the change is tracked: its PR, or its issue when it has one; the next session opens from that number.

The residue kept in place, which the canon does not carry: never compose a hand-off prompt, and this repo owner's opener. Shortened from three lines to two.

## Kept, after checking

- The `Proving a change` section against `basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md`'s eight new rules. The nearest pair are not the same rule: the canon's "assert it once in a sweep that reads the whole set out of the tree" is about *where* a set-wide assertion lives, and "pin how many members it covered" is about the count — neither says the local rule's point, that a sweep gathers every member's failure and asserts once at the end so one run reports them all.
- The local `github-api-via-shell` check against `claudinite-growth/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`'s new MCP-vs-`GITHUB_TOKEN` rule. A canon *check* would cover a local check; canon prose does not, and a check is the stronger form.
- `scheduler-workflows-are-thin` against `claudinite-lifecycle`'s `scheduler-workflow-shape`: complementary, not overlapping — one bans an inline program, the other asserts cron, dispatch, permissions and the entry point.
- `Reading a tool result the harness saved to a file` against `basics`' `github-list-without-fields`: the check prevents the dump, the local rule says how to read one that already exists.
- The five checks this window added (`tasks-stage-barriers`, `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`, `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface`, `tasks-retired-public-paths`, `repo-variables-through-the-bag`) enforce the tasks pack's own layout; no local item is about that.

## Verification
