{"number":2161,"title":"Claudinite growth: rule revalidation","body":"Weekly re-probe of the environment claims in this repo's **own local pack**
(`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/` — `RULES.md`, `references.md`, `declared-checks.json`
and `skills/running-the-suite/SKILL.md`). Canon packs under `packs/` are a different task's
corpus.

Run environment: node v22.22.2, git 2.43.0, shallow clone, unattended executor session scoped
to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only.

## One correction

**`running-the-suite`'s suite-command rule, `test-suite-command-form`'s `failureMessage`, and
`references.md` entry `running-the-suite-4`** — the rule said a bash glob without `globstar`
"reached 37 of 65 files and reported nothing wrong", and that *only the glob* leaves you
believing a green run.

Re-measured today:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `git ls-files '*.test.mjs' \| wc -l` | **314** tracked test files (was 65) |
| `shopt globstar` | `off` — the premise holds |
| `*.test.mjs` at the repo root, globstar off | expands to nothing; bash passes the literal |
| `node --test *.test.mjs` from the root | node expands the glob itself → `1..0`, `# tests 0`, **exit 1** |
| `node --test nosuchfile.test.mjs` | `Could not find 'nosuchfile.test.mjs'`, exit 1 |
| `node --test <dir>` | `Error: Cannot find module <dir>`, exit 1 — unchanged |
| `packs/*/test/*.test.mjs` | **125 of 314** files — runs, reports green |

So the sentence as written is now false for the shape it named: the root-level glob is loud, not
silent, because node v22 globs its own path arguments and finds nothing. The silent shape is the
glob that matches a *subset*, and that is what the rule, the check's message and the references
entry now say. The recommended command is unchanged.

## Every other claim, with its probe

### `holds`

- **`check:git-pull-on-shallow-clone`** — "the clones here are shallow". `git rev-parse
  --is-shallow-repository` → `true`.
- **`check:mount-path-in-the-canon-home`** — "the canon home carries no `.claudinite/shared/`".
  `ls -a .claudinite/` → `.gitattributes`, the two `GENERATED` files, `local`. No `shared`.
- **`check:checkout-restores-index`** — staged `edited-then-staged`, overwrote the working file,
  ran `git checkout -- <file>` in a scratch repo: the file came back as `edited-then-staged`, not
  the committed `one`. Restores from the index; the uncommitted edit was destroyed.
- **`check:github-api-via-shell`, `gh` arm** — `command -v gh` → absent from `PATH`. The entry's
  retirement condition requires *both* arms to flip, so retirement stays ruled out.
- **`check:hook-judges-never-exit`** — observed live: the PreToolUse judge held four calls this
  run at `exit=2` (`skill-not-loaded-for-call` ×3, `action-guard` ×1) and the harness rendered
  each as a block, while advisory judges returned context without exiting.
- **`check:shell-write-to-skill-scoped-path`** — observed live: two `> file` shell writes each
  produced the advisory as PostToolUse context, and neither was held pre-edit. The pre-edit guard
  still reads `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` only.
- **`check:year-last-digit-rollover`** — arithmetic; 2030's last digit is 0 and sorts below 2029's 9.
- **`check:commit-all-sweeps-edits`, `check:settings-json-reserialized`** — git and JSON semantics,
  unchanged.
- **`RULES-46`** (dotted version identifiers stay strings) — `Number('60820.10') === Number('60820.1')`
  → `true`.
- **Bash cwd reset** — call A ran `cd <scratchpad> && …` and ended with `Shell cwd was reset to
  /home/user/Claudinite`; call B's first `pwd` printed `/home/user/Claudinite`. The next call does
  start back at the root.
- **Reading a harness-saved tool result** — wrote a 3531-byte single-line JSON file and read it
  with `offset: 0, limit: 1`: the whole line came back. `python3 -c 'json.load(...)'` parsed the
  same file into 60 entries. Both halves of the rule stand.
- **`RULES-70`** (hook judges return, the runner exits) — `node dev/tools/hook-latency.mjs` runs and
  reports `exit 2` for held calls, `0` otherwise. Its p50s have drifted *down* since the entry's
  2026-09-05 measurement — pre 66 ms (Read, no declaration) and post 59 ms, against the recorded
  ~88 ms / ~80 ms. The entry is a dated before/after record of that change, so its numbers were left
  as the evidence they are; nothing the rule directs has changed.
- **`RULES-71` / `check:cross-repo-verify-line`, the session-scope half** — this session's GitHub
  scope names `missingbulb/Claudinite` and nothing else. The "probes fetch anonymously" half would
  need a cross-repo fetch and was not run.
- **`running-the-suite-4`** (`node --test <dir>` fails outright) — re-probed on the same node
  version; identical `Cannot find module` and exit 1.
- **`running-the-suite-1`, -2** — the suite ran green in **64 s** (3739 pass, 0 fail), close enough
  to the recorded "~55 s" that the directive is unaffected; `git ls-files '*.test.mjs'` omitted an
  unstaged new test file in a scratch repo and listed it after `git add`.

### `unprobed`

Left exactly as they stand — per the skill, a probe this session cannot run is not evidence the
claim is stale.

- **`check:github-api-via-shell`, the `api.github.com` arm** — the probe is a shell `curl` to
  `api.github.com`, which this repo's own blocking guard refuses. Its `gh` arm is probed and holds,
  so the check's standing is settled regardless; but the arm cannot be re-measured from a session
  the guard governs.
- **`RULES` on `Claude_Code_Remote`** and **`add_repo`** — `ToolSearch select:add_repo,Claude_Code_Remote`
  → "No matching deferred tools found", and a keyword search returned unrelated tools. Neither
  surface is provisioned in *this* session; that says nothing about the attended sessions the rules
  were written for.
- **`RULES-78`** (`EnterWorktree` denied after ~1 min unattended) — probing it would create a
  worktree and relocate this session's working directory mid-delivery, so probe rule 1 (read-only)
  bars it. `EnterWorktree` is present in this session's deferred roster, consistent with the rule's
  premise.
- **`RULES-73` / `check:subagent-branch-named-git`** — needs a worktree-isolated subagent; spawning
  one is outside this run's remit.
- **`check:busy-wait-loop`** ("the harness does not pre-empt a wedged Bash call") — the probe is
  wedging the session.
- **`check:author-association-as-permission`** — `doc-verified` was unavailable: `docs.github.com`
  is not on this environment's egress allowlist. `curl` returned `CONNECT tunnel failed, response
  403`, and `$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` confirms `connect_rejected … docs.github.com:443`.
  Per `fetching-from-the-web` a proxy denial is a policy boundary, so no sibling source was tried.
- **`RULES-38`** (~64 KB GitHub API field cap) — the probe is an oversized write. Same egress block
  rules out documentation as a substitute this run.
- **`RULES-82`** (a member's maintenance PR parked `action_required`) — the claim is about *member*
  repos' workflow-approval setting, which this session cannot reach. For what it is worth, the
  canon's own bot PR #2156 carries a single check run that executed to completion with no gated
  phantom beside it — consistent with the rule scoping the gate to members' settings rather than
  contradicting it.

## Incidental finding, not fixed here

`github-api-via-shell`'s matcher reads a `grep` **pattern** as a command: a search for
`"Claude_Code_Remote|add_repo|…|gh CLI"` was blocked because `|gh ` matches its
`(^|[;&|]\s*)…gh\s` alternation. It cost one retry this run and will recur for any session
grepping an alternation whose branch begins `gh `. Narrowing a blocking guard is not a
revalidation's call, so it is reported rather than changed.

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3739 pass, 0 fail, 64 s.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — clean, exit 0.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **0 blocking**, 232 advisory, all pre-existing
  whole-tree findings (`file-placement` reach, `rules-line-length` in `packs/node`,
  `design-doc-status-banner` on four `docs/` design docs).

{"number":2127,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Two `growth-extract` runs into the repo's own local pack. The branch is rebased onto `main` at `edd3bb8`.

## Run 2 — the 2026-09-20 window

Commits `ee10997`, `539352d`, the PRs merged in the window (#2116, #2135, #2136, #2166 and the task PRs), the issues touched in it, and the captures `2026-09-19T1943Z`–`2026-09-20T0957Z` plus the hindsight window `2026-07-19T1509Z`–`2026-07-20T1358Z`.

### `migration-record-paths-resolve` — a check

Every `packs/…` or `engine/…` path a migration record names as a literal must exist in the tree. Both directions a record uses such a path **fail open**: `appliesTo` reads an unreadable probe target as "not capable", and `applyMaterializations` skips a template it cannot read rather than clobber the destination with nothing. A layout move or a pack rename therefore turns the record inert with nothing going red.

`blocking`, `since: 2026-09-20`. The tree carries two violations and the check found both:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-09-05-task-cadence-terms/` probes `packs/claudinite-tasks/calendar.mjs`, which #1890 moved on 2026-09-14 leaving no shim — silently inert for thirteen days. That is #2139, which asks for exactly this sweep.
- `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/migrations/2026-08-05-sheepdog-fleet-baseline/` still materializes `packs/sheepdog/stubs/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml`, retired by the 2026-08-19 rename. Its sibling record's header says that template's deletion was deliberate, so what is left is a materialization that can never fire — a new finding, not covered by #2139's `src/<role>/` framing.

Red-first by mutation, since the declaration lands already finding the two: narrowing `inFilesMatching` to `packs/` turns the engine-side case red, and `scanIgnoringComments: false` turns the commented-out-declaration case red; each restored to green. Silent over the real tree's other 21 migration records.

### `RULES-95` — one rule, the whole prose ration

> **Putting a design, restructure or plan to the owner for approval** — render the end state whole, every element kind it touches rather than the one easiest to show, and name the decisions it took that they never asked about.

Three rounds in this window were the owner asking for exactly that, each on a proposal already written: on #2116, *"Explain again about the public folder, and contents. Describe specific files"* and then *"Now show me the final public folder layout with all files"*; on #2136, *"You didn't annotate skills and rules on the sample pack, just rules.md. I want to see how the pack will look after this transformation is done"* and then *"Highlight aspects that I didn't comment on or didn't ask for, so I won't be surprised by the solution"*. `basics`' approval submission names three things today — a line per step, the dependency graph, the policy per link — and neither of these.

It stays prose: the mark is the shape of a reply, and a check for it would be guessing at intent (class G).

### The upgrade pass

Nothing to convert — the run's only new prose is `RULES-95`, which has no artifact and no moment to hang a trigger on.

### What did not land, and why

- **#2135's "so many elements changed for a one-field flip"** — the owner's *"It seems like all places that you changes are either not needed, or are an indicate that there's much stronger coupling between elements"* is `basics`' *Handing over a change whose diff reached more folders or files than its request implied*, already in the corpus. The agent said so and then framed the width as justification rather than as the coupling report the rule asks for; that is under-execution of an existing rule, not a new one.
- **The hindsight window** re-read in full and yields nothing new: barriers-only tree segregation is `claudinite-canon-curation` RULES-12, "don't refer to other packs from packs" is `claudinite-growth` RULES-2, the cross-session prompt disclaimer is RULES-47, and "author the assurance first" is `basics`' own.
- **A note on that window:** #2135 took `logs-prune` off the schedule in this very window, so the branch's oldest end no longer moves and every future run re-reads these same six July captures. Not filed as an issue — the skill already calls reading more than the oldest window "only wasted effort", and the trade was the owner's deliberate call about data loss.

### Verification

Suite 3764/3764 after the rebase. `check_the_work` clean. `check_the_world` 0 blocking, 234 findings — the 232 standing on `main` plus this check's two.

## Run 1 — the 2026-09-18 window

`transcript-found-by-mtime` — an action guard on a Bash or Write call whose payload carries `mtime`, `projects` and `.jsonl` together, silent when it names `findTranscript` or `capture-log.mjs`. `blocking`, `since: 2026-09-18`.

The evidence is two firings of one mistake, two months apart:

- **2026-09-17, #2111.** The owner asked why a session had replied only `Comment class: process-change` and stopped. The transcript holding it belonged to an EdFringeNow session in another container, so the diagnostic went across as a script for that session to run. It chose its transcript as the newest `.jsonl` across every directory under `~/.claude/projects` — which is always the transcript of the session running the script. The receiving session reported back *"Only one transcript exists on this box and it is this session's own file, so the script diagnosed itself"*, listed the script's defects, and reproduced the case by hand anyway.

input.body:
Step 4 of #2169, the tail rather than a pack: five provenance files that no backfill run has reached, across three packs already backfilled.

Batched into one pull request per the owner's decision of 2026-09-21 — the batching test is how many pull requests a pack's elements arrived across, and these five arrived across four.

## Why they were missed

- `google-client-id-single-origin`, `python-optional-import-install-hint`, `python-optional-import-top-level` — each is declared behind a thin aggregator `checks.mjs`, which the original marking pass could not see through. #2248 taught the pass to follow an aggregator into the module that declares the id, which is what opened these three files; the packs' own backfills (#2216, #2217) had already run by then.

## PR #944 · 2026-08-17 · Claudinite growth: extract lessons
- by @missingbulb · model Claude
- the commit trailer references Refs #943 - READ THE PULL REQUEST BODY for the keyword it used and write that into Landed. the two disagree on most older pull requests, the body's Closes being what fills GitHub's Development panel and the trailer's Refs linking nothing there
- converging-unattended-run (born), excluding-files-vendor (reworded), pr-lands-squash (born), replying-owner-comment (born), restoring-source-deliberate (born), retiring-reshaping-protocol (born), testing-helper-reapplied (reworded), writing-generated-content (born)

> Growth-extract capture over the window in #943 — both halves: repo
> activity (16 commits, 15 merged PRs, 3 touched PRs, 14 touched issues)
> and captured conversation logs (18 sessions since retention makes no
> prune due). Lands 13 durable, non-duplicate lessons into this repo's
> own local pack, folded into existing bullets where they sharpen one and
> added new where the territory was genuinely uncovered — including a
> correction: the local "Waiting for something to happen" rule pointed
> at Monitor for GitHub CI status, which is proxy-blind here and was
> measured burning ~26 minutes across two PRs.

the defaults go under every entry below them; fill Source, Reason, Rejected and Retire when where the evidence carries them, there or on one entry; delete a draft the commit did not decide
```entry-defaults
- **Source:** the growth-extract run over the window in #943 - sixteen commits, fifteen merged
  pull requests and eighteen conversation captures.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #944 (Refs #943).
```
```entry converging-unattended-run
## 2026-08-17 · born · Claudinite growth: extract lessons (#944)
- **Reason:** two runs closed `outcome:done` with their own pull request still open and needing a
  human (#939, #892).
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule, triggered on "Converging an unattended run".
```
```entry excluding-files-vendor
## 2026-08-17 · reworded · Claudinite growth: extract lessons (#944)
- **Reason:** the whitelist test asserted the one file that had broken rather than its directory
  (#907).
```
```entry pr-lands-squash
## 2026-08-17 · born · Claudinite growth: extract lessons (#944)
- **Reason:** the head ref is deleted on squash-merge here, so the next push was rejected on a

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/running-the-suite

# Running the suite

- **The whole suite is one command** — `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. There is no test
  script; `ci.yml`'s array is not authoritative. A bash glob without `globstar` is the dangerous
  substitute — `packs/*/test/*.test.mjs` reports nothing wrong over 125 of 314 files — while
  `node --test <dir>` fails outright and a glob matching nothing exits 1, so only a glob that
  matches a subset leaves you believing a green run. (whole-suite-command)
- **Read a run's output from a file** — redirect one run and grep that file for the slice you need;
  never re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice unchanged output. (read-runs-output)
- **`git add` a new test file before certifying a run green** — `git ls-files` excludes an unstaged
  file, so the run never executed it; the `untracked-test-file` finding at Stop says which.
  (git-add-new)
- **Iterating on a sweep across many files** — run only the test files the edit touches, plus
  `check_the_work`; spend the whole suite and `check_the_world` once, at the end. Both are
  whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file. (iterating-sweep-across)
- **Editing a `RULES.md` or `README.md` under `packs/`** — the file that holds a pack's rule index
  in step with its prose sits outside the pack, and neither conformance sweep runs it, so add
  `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches. (editing-rules-md)

input.body:
Step 4 of the provenance backfill tracked in #2169, for one corpus: `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite`, the home repo's own local pack.

Refs #2169 — this is one step of that tracker, so it closes nothing.

## What landed

- **88 empty provenance files filled**, and history added to the files the references conversion had already filled. The folder goes from 93 entries to **341**; `find … -type f -empty` returns nothing.
- Derived from the pack's **153 pack-local commits**, the **58 pull request bodies** behind them read on GitHub, and the growth-extract tracker's per-run comments on #370.
- **6 declined candidates** recorded on `_declined.md` — the four rules the owner's review on #987 dropped, `history-test-shallow-guard` withdrawn in #1779, and the pack-README co-change check measured and not shipped in #2110.

## Where the brief's derivation was wrong

The brief's largest error is the two compaction passes, **#890** and **#1315**. Both re-keyed rules that already existed — #890's own body says *"57 bullets in, 57 out"* — but a rule reworded on its way across cannot be followed by its text, so the brief drafted **31 births at #890** and **38 at #1315** that are really rewordings.

Each was traced with a pickaxe over the pack's `RULES.md` at both paths the pack has lived at, against the pre-#890 file read out of the tree. Result: **48 births moved back** to the growth-extract run that actually landed each rule (#402 through #1290), and the drafts at #890/#1315 are `reworded`. The 17 that stayed born at #1315 are the clauses that became rules of their own there, each with the rule it was split out of.

Smaller ones: every drafted `reworded` on `consumer-safe-change` (#661, #776, #1338, #1850, #2060) and on `cross-repo-verify-line` and `bare-sleep-wait` is a `scope-changed` — what moved was the gate, not the words — and #1773's three are `severity-changed`.

## Landed keywords

The trailer and the body disagree on 18 of the 58 pull requests, and the body's keyword is what is written. #595 is the sharpest: the trailer says `Refs #592`, the body `Closes #593` — a different issue. #987 runs the other way, trailer `Closes #986` and body `Refs #986`.

## The manifest

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pack.mjs` | 1209 bytes | 510 bytes |
| `README.md` | — | the pack has none, so nothing to trim |

The header's decisions — why the pack exists, how discovery reaches it, what activates it, which check rides beside it — are `_pack` entries now; the header keeps what the pack is, in two lines. `_pack.md` also gains the #1674 scope change, where everything about the packs on the shelf left this pack for `claudinite-canon-curation`.

## Automerge

```
Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: under:.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/provenance; .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/pack.mjs
```

Predicted before the diff: the pack's `provenance/`, its `README.md` and its `pack.mjs`, and nothing else. The README turned out not to exist, so the diff is the other two.

## Verification

- `provenance.mjs check claudinite` — prints its 189-line file-to-carrier listing, no fault, exit 0.
- `find .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/provenance -type f -empty` — nothing.
- Whole suite: **3932 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, 26 advisory, none naming a file this change touches (the 78 `corpus-count-in-prose` findings an earlier draft raised are gone: the flagged rule count was dropped from the sentence that carried it).
- `check_the_work` — 0 blocking. Its advisories are `provenance-change-recorded` on the 48 files where an earlier born replaced the references conversion's placeholder, which is the case its own `fix` text names as correct.

## 2026-08-07 · born · growth-extract: two lessons from the 2026-08-05/06 window (#679)
- **Reason:** Where a change is uniform by construction — prose, a doc, a move of something
  nothing executes from the mount — forcing delivery buys noise rather than assurance; forcing is
  for changes whose behaviour turns on how members differ.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude, per the commit trailer.
- **Mechanism:** a RULES.md rule.
- **Retire when:** Retire the rule only if the nightly converge stops being the reliable delivery
  path.
- **Landed:** #679.

## 2026-08-16 · reworded · Rephrase the local pack's rules: trigger-keyed, and a third the words (#890)
- **Reason:** the file had grown to 57 claim-first entries over 622 lines and ~8,900 words, most a
  title followed by the narrative of the incident behind it. Every rule is re-keyed to the act that
  brings a reader to it, grouped by surface, and cut to the directive plus what it takes to obey it:
  622 lines / 8,870 words to 243 / 2,878, with no rule dropped, weakened or strengthened.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5, per the commit trailer.
- **Landed:** #890 (Closes #889).

## 2026-08-17 · reworded · Point every live Sheepdog-repo reference at Shepherd (#957)
- **Reason:** the fleet enforcer is now a separate repository, Shepherd; the retiring one is not a
  rename of it, so prose directing a session at the enforcer pointed at the wrong place.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).

Refs #2169 — this is one step of that tracker, so it closes nothing.

## What landed

- **88 empty provenance files filled**, and history added to the files the references conversion had already filled. The folder goes from 93 entries to **341**; `find … -type f -empty` returns nothing.
- Derived from the pack's **153 pack-local commits**, the **58 pull request bodies** behind them read on GitHub, and the growth-extract tracker's per-run comments on #370.
- **6 declined candidates** recorded on `_declined.md` — the four rules the owner's review on #987 dropped, `history-test-shallow-guard` withdrawn in #1779, and the pack-README co-change check measured and not shipped in #2110.

## Where the brief's derivation was wrong

The brief's largest error is the two compaction passes, **#890** and **#1315**. Both re-keyed rules that already existed — #890's own body says *"57 bullets in, 57 out"* — but a rule reworded on its way across cannot be followed by its text, so the brief drafted **31 births at #890** and **38 at #1315** that are really rewordings.

Each was traced with a pickaxe over the pack's `RULES.md` at both paths the pack has lived at, against the pre-#890 file read out of the tree. Result: **48 births moved back** to the growth-extract run that actually landed each rule (#402 through #1290), and the drafts at #890/#1315 are `reworded`. The 17 that stayed born at #1315 are the clauses that became rules of their own there, each with the rule it was split out of.

Smaller ones: every drafted `reworded` on `consumer-safe-change` (#661, #776, #1338, #1850, #2060) and on `cross-repo-verify-line` and `bare-sleep-wait` is a `scope-changed` — what moved was the gate, not the words — and #1773's three are `severity-changed`.

## Landed keywords

The trailer and the body disagree on 18 of the 58 pull requests, and the body's keyword is what is written. #595 is the sharpest: the trailer says `Refs #592`, the body `Closes #593` — a different issue. #987 runs the other way, trailer `Closes #986` and body `Refs #986`.

## The manifest

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pack.mjs` | 1209 bytes | 510 bytes |
| `README.md` | — | the pack has none, so nothing to trim |

The header's decisions — why the pack exists, how discovery reaches it, what activates it, which check rides beside it — are `_pack` entries now; the header keeps what the pack is, in two lines. `_pack.md` also gains the #1674 scope change, where everything about the packs on the shelf left this pack for `claudinite-canon-curation`.

## Automerge

```
Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: under:.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/provenance; .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/pack.mjs
```

Predicted before the diff: the pack's `provenance/`, its `README.md` and its `pack.mjs`, and nothing else. The README turned out not to exist, so the diff is the other two.

## Verification

- `provenance.mjs check claudinite` — prints its 189-line file-to-carrier listing, no fault, exit 0.
- `find .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/provenance -type f -empty` — nothing.
- Whole suite: **3932 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, 26 advisory, none naming a file this change touches (the 78 `corpus-count-in-prose` findings an earlier draft raised are gone: the flagged rule count was dropped from the sentence that carried it).
- `check_the_work` — 0 blocking. Its advisories are `provenance-change-recorded` on the 48 files where an earlier born replaced the references conversion's placeholder, which is the case its own `fix` text names as correct.

Both PRs are up and the fan-out is cleared.

**[missingbulb/Claudinite#2265](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2265) — Provenance: backfill the home's local pack**

```
.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/      88 empty files filled, history added to the ones
  provenance/                            the references conversion had already filled; folder
                                         goes 93 → 341 entries, plus 6 declined candidates
.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/      manifest header trimmed 1209 → 510 bytes; its
  pack.mjs                               decisions moved onto _pack.md as entries
```

141 files, 2330 insertions. I verified rather than relayed: the pushed branch touches only those two paths (nothing in `packs/`), zero files on it are empty, and zero `born` entries still cite #890 — which was the agent's biggest claimed correction.

That correction is the part worth your attention. The brief drafted **69 births across #890 and #1315**, two compaction passes that #890's own body says re-keyed existing rules *"57 bullets in, 57 out"*. A rule reworded on its way across can't be followed by its text, so the tool had no way to see this — and it did **not** flag them under *births the search could not go behind*. 48 births moved back to the growth-extract runs that actually landed them. The 17 kept at #1315 are clauses that genuinely became rules there.

Second thing: trailer and body disagree on the closing keyword in **18 of 58** PRs. #595 is the sharp one — trailer `Refs #592`, body `Closes #593`, a *different issue*. Writing the trailer's would have cited the wrong issue 18 times.

Both PRs reference #2169 without closing it. #2265's CI is still running (`unstable`); #2263 is fresh. I'm not polling either — I'll act on events if they arrive.

> ⚠️ Still open: `basics` (129 files, 1.05 MB brief) and `claudinite-growth` (87, 440 KB) are unstarted, as you asked. When you want them, the same one-agent-per-corpus shape applies, and the #890/#1315 finding above should go into the prompt — that failure mode is corpus-wide, so `basics` and `claudinite-growth` will have their own compaction passes drafting false births.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- extract-from-instructions: Convert instruction prose somebody already wrote into pack carriers, leaving the prose file a thin routing map. Use when adopting Claudinite on a repo that already carries a CLAUDE.md, when a person wants their machine-local instructions carried properly, or when asked to convert instruction prose into a pack.
- extract-packs-from-a-project: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve a repo's own comments as a pass of their own: delete, correct, add the why. Use when working a repo's comments deliberately (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner approves the current branch or PR, or asks to merge or land it into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production. Use when designing a larger element, when filing a migration plan's chain, when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. - running-the-suite: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- triaging-usage-findings: Turn a usage-review finding that has lasted into a proposed change - read the element's provenance first, settle which of the rule's causes it is, and write the edit itself rather than a description of it. - unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: How a plan's phases are ordered so nothing stalls mid-run. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan (including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file), when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written - RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon - brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, the marker that names a rule's provenance file. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments.
